```lua
        -- a 2.0 theme names its layers (backgroundLayers / foregroundLayers: sprite, parallax, scale, looping); they are
        -- given to the engine in the older order ({sheet, sprite, speed, scale, looping}) that Friends 1.0 used
        setTheme = function(theme)
            local t = env.blockTable and env.blockTable.themes and env.blockTable.themes[theme]
            if type(t) == "table" and t.bgLayers == nil then
                local function layers(list)
                    local out = {}
                    for i, l in ipairs(list or {}) do out[i] = {"", l.sprite, l.parallax or 0, l.scale or 1, l.looping ~= false} end
                    return out
                end
                t.bgLayers, t.fgLayers = layers(t.backgroundLayers), layers(t.foregroundLayers)
            end
            env.setTheme(theme)
        end,
        drawBackground = function() env.drawBackgroundNative() end,
        drawForeground = function() env.drawForegroundNative() end,
        createThemeSprite = function(name, sprite, x, y, speedX, scaleX, scaleY, angle, layer)
            env.createThemeSprite(name, sprite, x, y, scaleX or 1, scaleY or 1, angle or 0, speedX or 0, layer or 0)
        end,
        setThemeRectColour = function() end,
    }),
    DebugConsoleNative = module("DebugConsoleNative", {getInput = function() return "" end, activate = function() end, deactivate = function() end}),
}

-- the picture groups (native.ResourceManager): Assets.lua names each group's files (a sprite sheet .dat = 0, a set of
-- composite sprites = 1) with setGroup, then acquires and releases groups by name; a group is loaded on its first acquire
-- and freed when the last holder lets go
do
    local groups, holders = {}, {}
    local function each(name, sheet, compo)
        local g = groups[name]
        if not g then return end
        for _, f in ipairs(g.files) do
            local file = g.path .. "/" .. tostring(f[1])
            local fn = (f[2] == 0 and sheet) or (f[2] == 1 and compo)
            if fn then local ok, err = pcall(fn, file) if not ok then print("friends 2.0.0: " .. file .. ": " .. tostring(err)) end end
        end
    end
    local manager = {requiredTextureMemory = 0, usedTextureMemory = 0}
    manager.setMemoryLimit = function() end
    manager.setGroup = function(name, path, files) groups[name] = {path = path, files = files or {}} end
    manager.acquireGroup = function(name)
        holders[name] = (holders[name] or 0) + 1
        if holders[name] == 1 then each(name, res.createSpriteSheet, res.createCompoSpriteSet) end
    end
    manager.releaseGroup = function(name)
        if not holders[name] then return end
        holders[name] = holders[name] - 1
        if holders[name] <= 0 then holders[name] = nil each(name, res.releaseSpriteSheet, res.releaseCompoSpriteSet) end
    end
    manager.isGroupLoaded = function(name) return holders[name] ~= nil end
    if type(env.native) == "table" then env.native.ResourceManager = module("ResourceManager", manager) end
    -- the phone knew every group's sprites from the start (only the pictures waited for acquireGroup): a frame made before its group
    -- is taken (the game HUD's slingshot menu measures SLINGSHOT_TAB_LEFT / _BOTTOM_LEFT when it is built) gets the sizes from the files
    local peeked = {}
    local function peek(sprite)
        local known = peeked[sprite]
        if known then if known[1] then return known[1], known[2], known[3], known[4] end return end
        peeked[sprite] = {}
        for _, g in pairs(groups) do
            for _, f in ipairs(g.files) do
                if f[2] == 0 and env.res.abPeekSprite then
                    local w, h, px, py = env.res.abPeekSprite(g.path .. "/" .. tostring(f[1]), sprite)
                    if w then peeked[sprite] = {w, h, px, py} return w, h, px, py end
                end
            end
        end
    end
    local wrapped = false
    local function wrap()   -- done when the game names its first group: the game's res table is there by then
        local r = rawget(env, "res")
        if wrapped or type(r) ~= "table" or type(r.getSpriteBounds) ~= "function" then return end
        wrapped = true
        local bounds, pivot = r.getSpriteBounds, r.getSpritePivot
        r.getSpriteBounds = function(a, b)
            local w, h = bounds(a, b)
            if w == 0 and h == 0 then local pw, ph = peek(b or a) if pw then return pw, ph end end
            return w, h
        end
        r.getSpritePivot = function(a, b)
            local x, y = pivot(a, b)
            if x == 0 and y == 0 then local w, h, px, py = peek(b or a) if w then return px, py end end
            return x, y
        end
    end
    local setGroup = manager.setGroup
    manager.setGroup = function(...) wrap() return setGroup(...) end
end

-- the phone tells the game its screen size once it is known (g_updatedScreenWidth/Height); update() then sets
-- g_assetSizeX/Y (updateAssetSizes), which every menu scales by
env.g_updatedScreenWidth, env.g_updatedScreenHeight = env.screenWidth, env.screenHeight

-- a resized window: the phone's screen never changed size, so a page keeps the size it was built at (the login page / main
-- menu sets w, h = screenWidth, screenHeight once). The pages made at an earlier window size take the new one before the
-- game lays them out again (MenuManager:update does that when screenWidth changes, setRoot when a page is shown)
do
    local old = {}
    local function fit(frame, seen)
        if type(frame) ~= "table" or seen[frame] then return end
        seen[frame] = true
        local w, h = rawget(frame, "w"), rawget(frame, "h")
        if type(w) == "number" and type(h) == "number" and old[w .. "x" .. h] and (w ~= env.screenWidth or h ~= env.screenHeight) then
            frame.w, frame.h = env.screenWidth, env.screenHeight
        end
        local children = rawget(frame, "children")
        if type(children) == "table" then for _, c in pairs(children) do fit(c, seen) end end
    end
    env.abWindowResized = function(ow, oh)
        old[ow .. "x" .. oh] = true
        local m = env.menuManager
        if type(m) ~= "table" then return end
        if type(m.menus) == "table" then local seen = {} for _, f in pairs(m.menus) do fit(f, seen) end end
        if rawget(m, "setRoot") == nil and type(m.setRoot) == "function" then
            local setRoot = m.setRoot
            m.setRoot = function(self, frame, ...) fit(frame, {}) return setRoot(self, frame, ...) end
        end
    end
end

-- loadTableFromFile(file, name): a saved file (highscores.lua) read again into the global `name` (at a tournament rollover)
if env.loadTableFromFile == nil then
    env.loadTableFromFile = function(file, name)
        local ok, t = pcall(env.loadPersistentFileWrapper, file)
        if ok and type(t) == "table" then env[name] = t end
    end
end

-- text in several fonts (MultiFontText): the bitmap fonts here are taken to have every letter the text needs
if env.doesFontHaveRequiredGlyphs == nil then env.doesFontHaveRequiredGlyphs = function() return true end end
if env.splitMultiFontText == nil then env.splitMultiFontText = function(text, font) return {{text = text or "", font = font}} end end

-- its createCircle has no collision flag: (name, sprite, x, y, radius, density, friction, restitution, controllable, zOrder, 0)
env.abCircleNoCollision = true

-- a first start has no highscores.lua: the phone gives the game an empty table
if env.highscores == nil then env.highscores = {} end

-- the phone build (the engine's debug keys turn the cheats on later, with the game's DebugConsole.lua)
if rawget(env, "releaseBuild") == nil then env.releaseBuild = true end

-- behind the globals: the environment's (and the real global table's) fallback finds these when the name is not a global
local function behind(t)
    local mt = getmetatable(t)
    if not mt then mt = {} setmetatable(t, mt) end
    local old = mt.__index
    mt.__index = function(tbl, k)
        local v = natives[k]
        if v ~= nil then return v end
        if type(old) == "function" then return old(tbl, k) end
        if type(old) == "table" then return old[k] end
    end
end
behind(env)
if _G ~= env then behind(_G) end

```

`src/lua/friends_server.lua`:

```lua
-- Angry Birds Friends: a stand-in for the game's server, so the online part plays on this computer.
--
-- The phone game talked to Rovio's and Facebook's servers for the login, the Weekly Tournament, the coins, the
-- power-up shop and the daily rewards (the native `facebook` table). None of that exists any more. This file answers
-- those calls locally: "Log in with Facebook" logs in a local player, the tournament runs on the levels the game ships
-- (levels/pack57, six a week, the week ending on Monday at midnight), and the score lists hold the player and the two
-- bots of the offline game: Red Bird scores each level's three-star score (goldScore) and the Yellow Bird its two-star
-- score (silverScore), and their tournament totals are the sums over the week's levels. Coins, power-ups bought with them,
-- trophies and the daily reward streak are kept in settings.lua (settings.abServer). Prices and rewards are made up: the
-- real ones came from the server.
--
-- Run by the engine inside the game's environment after its offline `facebook` stand-in is made (script_host.cpp).

local env = ...
local fb = _G.facebook
if type(fb) ~= "table" or not rawget(fb, "abOffline") then return end

local floor, max, min = math.floor, math.max, math.min

local CODES = {1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 15, 16, 20, 24, 26, 27, 41, 56, 57, 58, 60, 61, 126, 128, 130, 131, 132, 133, 135, 136, 137, 139, 140, 155}
local LEVELS_PER_WEEK = 6
local WEEK = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60
local EPOCH = os.time({year = 2013, month = 4, day = 29, hour = 0})     -- a Monday at midnight: weeks run Monday to Monday
local LOGIN_GIFT = 200
local PODIUM_COINS = {30, 20, 10}
local STAR_COINS = {2, 4, 8}

-- the power-up shop (buy code -> the item names it gives) and its prices: tq = how many, p = coins, fq = how many free
local ITEMS = {BirdFood = {"superseed"}, ExtraSpeed = {"kingsling"}, LaserSight = {"slingscope"}, Earthquake = {"birdquake"},
               ExtraBird = {"extrabird"}, PowerupBundle = {"superseed", "kingsling", "slingscope", "birdquake"}}
local PRICES = {
    BirdFood = {{tq = 3, p = 30, fq = 0}, {tq = 10, p = 90, fq = 1}, {tq = 25, p = 200, fq = 5}},
    ExtraSpeed = {{tq = 3, p = 30, fq = 0}, {tq = 10, p = 90, fq = 1}, {tq = 25, p = 200, fq = 5}},
    LaserSight = {{tq = 3, p = 30, fq = 0}, {tq = 10, p = 90, fq = 1}, {tq = 25, p = 200, fq = 5}},
    Earthquake = {{tq = 3, p = 30, fq = 0}, {tq = 10, p = 90, fq = 1}, {tq = 25, p = 200, fq = 5}},
    ExtraBird = {{tq = 1, p = 30, fq = 0}, {tq = 5, p = 130, fq = 1}},
    PowerupBundle = {{tq = 3, p = 100, fq = 0}, {tq = 10, p = 300, fq = 2}},
}
local DAILY = {{day = 1, itemId = "BirdFood", quantity = 1}, {day = 2, itemId = "ExtraSpeed", quantity = 1}, {day = 3, itemId = "LaserSight", quantity = 1},
               {day = 4, itemId = "Earthquake", quantity = 1}, {day = 5, itemId = "VirtualCurrency", quantity = 20}}

local mode = "offline"
local playerUpdateCallback, timeoutCallback
local countdown                                      -- the tutorial tournament's last seconds: {ends = time, done = function}

-- a server answers later, never inside the call: the menus count on that (an answer given at once opened the results
-- window in the middle of the frame that made it, before it was set up). Answers wait for the next frame.
local queue, flushing = {}, false
local function flush()
    local jobs = queue
    queue = {}
    for _, job in ipairs(jobs) do
        local ok, err = pcall(job.fn, unpack(job.args, 1, job.n))
        if not ok then print("friends server: " .. tostring(err)) end
    end
end
local function later(fn, ...)
    if type(fn) ~= "function" then return end
    local engine = env.engine or _G.engine
    if not (engine and engine.on) then fn(...) return end
    if not flushing then flushing = true engine.on("update", flush) end
    queue[#queue + 1] = {fn = fn, args = {...}, n = select("#", ...)}
end

-- the saved state, in the game's own settings table
local function state()
    local settings = env.settings
    if type(settings) ~= "table" then return {coins = 0, scores = {}, trophies = {0, 0, 0}, daily = {}} end
    local s = settings.abServer
    if type(s) ~= "table" then s = {} settings.abServer = s end
    s.coins = s.coins or 0
    s.scores = s.scores or {}
    s.trophies = s.trophies or {0, 0, 0}
    s.daily = s.daily or {}
    return s
end
local function save()
    if env.saveLuaFileWrapper then pcall(env.saveLuaFileWrapper, "settings.lua", "settings", true) end
end
local function notify(name)
    local ev = env.friendsEvents and env.friendsEvents[name]
    if ev and env.eventManager then pcall(env.eventManager.notify, env.eventManager, {id = ev}) end
end

local function weekNumber() return floor((os.time() - EPOCH) / WEEK) end
local function weekCodes(week)
    local list, first = {}, (week % (#CODES / LEVELS_PER_WEEK)) * LEVELS_PER_WEEK
    for i = 1, LEVELS_PER_WEEK do list[i] = "2000-" .. CODES[first + i] end
    return list
end

local function addCoins(n)
    local s = state()
    s.coins = max(0, s.coins + n)
    notify("EID_CREDIT_COUNT_UPDATED")
end
local function addItem(name, n)
    local wrapper = env.settingsWrapper
    if not (wrapper and wrapper.getItem) then return 0 end
    local item = wrapper:getItem(name)
    item.totalCount = (item.totalCount or 0) + n
    return item.totalCount - (item.usedCount or 0)
end
local function giveReward(itemId, quantity)
    if itemId == "VirtualCurrency" then addCoins(quantity) return end
    for _, name in ipairs(ITEMS[itemId] or {}) do addItem(name, quantity) end
end

-- the score lists: the player against the two bots, best first
local function scoreList(own, red, yellow)
    local list = {{id = "-1", name = "Red Bird", points = red, isBot = true}, {id = "-2", name = "Yellow Bird", points = yellow, isBot = true},
                  {id = "0", name = "Player", points = own, isOwnPlayer = true}}
    table.sort(list, function(a, b) if a.points ~= b.points then return a.points > b.points end return a.isOwnPlayer == true end)
    local ownRank = 1
    for i, e in ipairs(list) do
        e.rank = i e.stars = 0 e.invite = false e.gift = false
        e.isBot = e.isBot or false e.isOwnPlayer = e.isOwnPlayer or false
        e.firstName = e.name e.lastName = ""
        if e.isOwnPlayer then ownRank = i end
    end
    return list, ownRank
end
local function weekTotal()
    local total = 0
    for _, code in ipairs(weekCodes(state().week or weekNumber())) do total = total + (state().scores[code] or 0) end
    return total
end
local function botTotals(levels)       -- the bots' totals over a list of level names (Red Bird: three-star scores, Yellow Bird: two-star scores)
    local red, yellow = 0, 0
    for _, level in ipairs(levels) do local gold, silver = fb.starScores(level) red = red + gold yellow = yellow + silver end
    return red, yellow
end
local function tournamentList()
    local levels = {}
    for i, code in ipairs(weekCodes(state().week or weekNumber())) do levels[i] = "Level" .. code end
    return scoreList(weekTotal(), botTotals(levels))
end

-- a new week: the last one's standings become the results (trophies and coins for the podium), the scores start again
local function rollover()
    local s, week = state(), weekNumber()
    if s.week == nil then s.week = week return end
    if s.week >= week then return end
    if weekTotal() > 0 then
        local players, rank = tournamentList()
        local reward = PODIUM_COINS[rank] or 0
        if rank <= 3 then s.trophies[rank] = s.trophies[rank] + 1 end
        local result = {valid = true, ownRank = rank, ownPoints = weekTotal(), players = players,
                        goldTrophies = s.trophies[1], silverTrophies = s.trophies[2], bronzeTrophies = s.trophies[3],
                        prizeCounts = {s.trophies[1], s.trophies[2], s.trophies[3], 0, 0},
                        rewardItemId = reward > 0 and "VirtualCurrency" or "", rewardQuantity = reward}
        if reward > 0 then addCoins(reward) end
        s.lastResult = result
        s.lastResultSeen = false
    end
    s.week = week
    s.scores = {}
    save()
    later(timeoutCallback)
end

-- a cleared tournament level counts for this week's standings
local hooked = false
local listener = {name = "abFriendsServer"}
function listener:eventTriggered(event)
    if not (env.events and event.id == env.events.EID_LEVEL_ENDED and event.levelComplete and mode == "online") then return end
    local code = string.match(tostring(event.level), "Level([%w%-]+)$")
    for _, c in ipairs(weekCodes(state().week or weekNumber())) do
        if c == code then
            local s = state()
            -- coins for the stars that are new this week: 2 for the first, 4 for the second, 8 for the third (the level end screen shows them)
            if env.getStarCount then
                local before = (s.scores[c] or 0) > 0 and env.getStarCount(event.level, s.scores[c]) or 0
                local now = env.getStarCount(event.level, event.score or 0) or 0
                for star = before + 1, now do addCoins(STAR_COINS[star] or 0) end
            end
            s.scores[c] = max(s.scores[c] or 0, event.score or 0)
            save()
            later(playerUpdateCallback)
        end
    end
end
local function hook()
    if hooked or not (env.eventManager and env.events and env.events.EID_LEVEL_ENDED) then return end
    hooked = true
    env.eventManager:addEventListener(env.events.EID_LEVEL_ENDED, listener)
end

    if state().coins < price.p then later(cb, false, nil, "Not enough coins.") return end

end
```

`src/lua/hatchery_natives.lua`:

```lua
-- Angry Birds Island HD (Hatchery) tile manager.
--
-- The iOS game draws the Hatchery with a native "TileManager" (createHatcheryMap, createNewTileObject,
-- screenToTileWorld ...). The iOS binary is the only place those natives exist, and its VFP arithmetic does not
-- disassemble reliably, so this is a re-implementation from the scripts' own use of the calls and from the map
-- data (a Tiled isometric map of 70x70 tiles, 196x97 pixels each). initializeTileManager(w, h, size) receives
-- size = (tilewidth - 3) * sin(45 deg) = 136.5: the side of one tile in world units. The view is the usual
-- 2:1 isometric projection of that square grid.
--
-- Run by the engine inside the game's environment, so `gamelua` is that environment.

local env = ...
local floor, sqrt, sin, cos, min, max, abs = math.floor, math.sqrt, math.sin, math.cos, math.min, math.max, math.abs
local C45 = 0.70710678118654752

local tm = nil            -- the tile manager state (nil until initializeTileManager)

local function screenSize()
    return env.screenWidth or 1024, env.screenHeight or 768
end

-- ---- drawing ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The engine's render state scales and moves everything by (position + translation) * scale, i.e. about the screen's
-- origin, not about the sprite. To draw a sprite with its pivot at (x, y), scaled and turned about that pivot, the state's
-- translation is (x / sx, y / sy) and its pivot is the sprite's own pivot (drawn at (0, 0)).
local function blit(name, x, y, sx, sy, angle, alpha)
    alpha = alpha or 1
    if sx == 0 or sy == 0 or alpha <= 0 then return end
    if sx == 1 and sy == 1 and angle == 0 and alpha == 1 then
        res.drawSprite("", name, x, y)
        return
    end
    local px, py = res.getSpritePivot("", name)
    env.setRenderState(x / sx, y / sy, sx, sy, angle, px, py, alpha)
    res.drawSprite("", name, 0, 0)
    env.setRenderState(0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1)
end

-- ---- projection ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- world (square grid, units of `size` per tile) <-> unscaled projection <-> screen
local function project(wx, wy)
    return (wx - wy) * C45, (wx + wy) * C45 * 0.5
end

local function unproject(px, py)
    local a, b = px / C45, py / (C45 * 0.5)       -- a = wx - wy, b = wx + wy
    return (a + b) * 0.5, (b - a) * 0.5
end

local function worldToScreen(wx, wy)
    local sw, sh = screenSize()
    local px, py = project(wx, wy)
    local cx, cy = project(tm.camX, tm.camY)
    return sw * 0.5 + (px - cx) * tm.scale, sh * 0.5 + (py - cy) * tm.scale
end

local function screenToWorld(x, y)
    local sw, sh = screenSize()
    local cx, cy = project(tm.camX, tm.camY)
    return unproject((x - sw * 0.5) / tm.scale + cx, (y - sh * 0.5) / tm.scale + cy)
end

local function clampCamera()
    tm.camX = max(0, min(tm.w * tm.size, tm.camX))
    tm.camY = max(0, min(tm.h * tm.size, tm.camY))
end

-- ---- animations ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- hatcheryAnimations[name] = { anchor = {x, y}, frames = { {time, x, y, scaleX, scaleY, rotation, easing}, ... } }
-- time is in seconds (the last frame's time is the length); x moves the sprite right, y UP in pixels (a jump is positive y); scale and rotation turn
-- about the anchor, a point of the sprite given as fractions of its size from the top left (it may lie outside the sprite).
-- easing: 1 = ease out (decelerates), -1 = ease in (accelerates), 0/nil = linear (applied to the segment that starts at that frame)
local animations = {}

local function ease(t, e)
    if e == 1 then return 1 - (1 - t) * (1 - t) end      -- eases out: fast at the start, slow at the end
    if e == -1 then return t * t end                     -- eases in
    return t
end

local function sampleAnimation(anim, t)
    local f = anim.frames
    local n = #f
    if n == 0 then return 0, 0, 1, 1, 0 end
    if t <= f[1].time then local a = f[1]; return a.x or 0, a.y or 0, a.scaleX or 1, a.scaleY or 1, a.rotation or 0 end
    for i = 1, n - 1 do
        local a, b = f[i], f[i + 1]
        if t <= b.time then
            local k = (t - a.time) / max(b.time - a.time, 1e-6)
            k = ease(k, a.easing)
            local function mix(p, q, d) p = p or d; q = q or d; return p + (q - p) * k end
            return mix(a.x, b.x, 0), mix(a.y, b.y, 0), mix(a.scaleX, b.scaleX, 1), mix(a.scaleY, b.scaleY, 1), mix(a.rotation, b.rotation, 0)
        end
    end
    local a = f[n]
    return a.x or 0, a.y or 0, a.scaleX or 1, a.scaleY or 1, a.rotation or 0
end

local function animationLength(anim)
    local f = anim.frames
    return (#f > 0 and f[#f].time) or 0
end

function env.createAnimation(id, def)
    animations[id] = def
end

-- ---- tile objects -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- an object: { id, sprites = { {name, ox, oy, sx, sy, angle} }, w, h (tiles), worldX, worldY, placed, selected,
--              anims = { {id, loop, speed, time} }, renderQueue, type, collision, selectable, children = { object } }
local objects = {}
local nextId = 1
local placed = {}       -- list of placed objects (not the ones inside a container)

local function snapPosition(o, wx, wy)
    local s = tm.size
    return (floor(wx / s) + 0.5 * (o.w or 1)) * s, (floor(wy / s) + 0.5 * (o.h or 1)) * s
end

-- the zero based tile indices an object centred at (wx, wy) covers
local function footprint(o, wx, wy)
    local s = tm.size
    local w, h = o.w or 1, o.h or 1
    local i0 = floor(wx / s - w * 0.5 + 0.5)
    local j0 = floor(wy / s - h * 0.5 + 0.5)
    return i0, j0, i0 + w - 1, j0 + h - 1
end

function env.initializeTileManager(w, h, size)
    tm = { w = w, h = h, size = size, scale = 1, camX = w * size * 0.5, camY = h * size * 0.5,
           base = {}, decorations = {}, defs = {} }
    objects, placed, nextId = {}, {}, 1
end

function env.deinitializeTileManager()
    tm = nil
    objects, placed = {}, {}
end

function env.createNewTileObject(params)
    local id = nextId
    nextId = nextId + 1
    local o = { id = id, sprites = {}, w = params.width or 1, h = params.height or 1, anims = {}, selected = false,
                renderQueue = params.renderQueue or 0, type = params.type, static = params.static,
                collision = params.collision, selectable = params.selectable, worldX = 0, worldY = 0, children = {} }
    for i, s in ipairs(params.sprites or {}) do o.sprites[i] = { name = s, ox = 0, oy = 0, sx = 1, sy = 1, angle = 0 } end
    objects[id] = o
    return id
end

local function leaveContainers(o)
    for _, p in pairs(objects) do
        for i = #p.children, 1, -1 do if p.children[i] == o then table.remove(p.children, i) end end
    end
end

function env.removeTileObjectFromLocation(id)
    local o = objects[id]
    if not o or not o.placed then return end
    o.placed = false
    for i = #placed, 1, -1 do if placed[i] == o then table.remove(placed, i) break end end
end

function env.removeTileObject(id)
    local o = objects[id]
    if not o then return end
    env.removeTileObjectFromLocation(id)
    leaveContainers(o)
    objects[id] = nil
end

function env.addTileObjectToLocation(id, wx, wy, snap)
    local o = objects[id]
    if not o or not tm then return end
    if snap == false then o.worldX, o.worldY = wx, wy else o.worldX, o.worldY = snapPosition(o, wx, wy) end
    if not o.placed then
        o.placed = true
        placed[#placed + 1] = o
    end
end

function env.setTileObjectSprites(id, sprites)
    local o = objects[id]
    if not o then return end
    o.sprites = {}
    for i, s in ipairs(sprites or {}) do o.sprites[i] = { name = s, ox = 0, oy = 0, sx = 1, sy = 1, angle = 0 } end
end

function env.setTileObjectType(id, t) if objects[id] then objects[id].type = t end end

function env.addSpriteToTileObject(id, name)
    local o = objects[id]
    if o then o.sprites[#o.sprites + 1] = { name = name, ox = 0, oy = 0, sx = 1, sy = 1, angle = 0 } end
end

-- sprite indices are zero based in the scripts
function env.removeSpriteFromTileObject(id, index)
    local o = objects[id]
    if o and o.sprites[index + 1] then table.remove(o.sprites, index + 1) end
end

function env.setSpriteParameters(id, index, ox, oy, sx, sy, angle)
    local o = objects[id]
    local s = o and o.sprites[index + 1]
    if s then s.ox, s.oy, s.sx, s.sy, s.angle = ox or 0, oy or 0, sx or 1, sy or 1, angle or 0 end
end

function env.addAnimationToTileObject(id, params)
    local o = objects[id]
    if o then o.anims[#o.anims + 1] = { id = params.id, loop = params.loop, speed = params.speed or 1, time = 0 } end
end

function env.removeAnimationFromTileObject(id, animId)
    local o = objects[id]
    if not o then return end
    for i = #o.anims, 1, -1 do if o.anims[i].id == animId then table.remove(o.anims, i) end end
end

function env.removeAllAnimationsFromTileObject(id)
    if objects[id] then objects[id].anims = {} end
end

function env.setObjectSelected(id, on)
    if objects[id] then objects[id].selected = on and true or false end
end

-- an egg or a bird in a nest is drawn with the nest, at its place (and does not stand on the map by itself)
function env.addObjectToContainerObject(childId, parentId)
    local child, parent = objects[childId], objects[parentId]
    if not child or not parent then return end
    env.removeTileObjectFromLocation(childId)
    leaveContainers(child)
    parent.children = { child }          -- a nest holds one thing: a bird takes the place of the egg it hatched from
end

-- ---- camera and coordinate conversion -------------------------------------------------------------------------
function env.setTileMapScale(s) if tm then tm.scale = max(0.1, min(4, s)) end end

function env.setTileCameraPosition(x, y)
    if not tm then return end
    tm.camX, tm.camY = x, y
    clampCamera()
end

function env.getTileCameraPosition()
    if not tm then return 0, 0 end
    return tm.camX, tm.camY
end

-- dragging by (dx, dy) screen pixels moves the camera the other way
function env.moveTileCameraPosition(dx, dy)
    if not tm then return end
    local sw, sh = screenSize()
    local ax, ay = screenToWorld(sw * 0.5 - dx, sh * 0.5 - dy)
    tm.camX, tm.camY = ax, ay
    clampCamera()
end

-- with snap (the third argument) the position becomes the centre of the tile it is in
function env.screenToTileWorld(x, y, snap)
    if not tm then return 0, 0 end
    local wx, wy = screenToWorld(x, y)
    if snap and snap ~= 0 and snap ~= false then
        local s = tm.size
        wx, wy = (floor(wx / s) + 0.5) * s, (floor(wy / s) + 0.5) * s
    end
    return wx, wy
end

function env.tileWorldToScreen(wx, wy) if not tm then return 0, 0 end return worldToScreen(wx, wy) end

-- centre of the tile with the given (zero based) indices
function env.getWorldCoordinatesForTileMapIndexes(ix, iy)
    return (floor(ix) + 0.5) * tm.size, (floor(iy) + 0.5) * tm.size
end

-- Tiled isometric object coordinates are in units of the tile height
function env.convertFromTILEDCoordinates(x, y)
    local th = tm.tileHeight or 97
    return x / th * tm.size, y / th * tm.size
end

-- ---- the map -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function env.createHatcheryMap(map, defs)
    tm.defs = defs
    tm.tileHeight = map.tileHeight
    tm.base = map.layers.Base and map.layers.Base.data or {}
    tm.decorations = {}
    tm.blocked = {}
    local deco = map.layers.Decoration and map.layers.Decoration.objects or {}
    for _, d in ipairs(deco) do
        local def = defs[tostring(d.gid)]
        local wx, wy = env.convertFromTILEDCoordinates(d.x, d.y)
        if def and def.sprites and def.sprites[1] then
            tm.decorations[#tm.decorations + 1] = { name = def.sprites[1], wx = wx, wy = wy, depth = wx + wy, queue = def.renderQueue or 0 }
            if def.collision == true then
                local ix, iy = floor(wx / tm.size), floor(wy / tm.size)
                tm.blocked[iy * tm.w + ix + 1] = true
            end
        end
    end
    -- the view starts over the land (the middle of the tiles that are not water or cliff)
    local sx, sy, n = 0, 0, 0
    for idx, gid in ipairs(tm.base) do
        local def = gid ~= 0 and defs[tostring(gid)]
        if def and def.collision ~= true then
            local i, j = (idx - 1) % tm.w, floor((idx - 1) / tm.w)
            sx, sy, n = sx + i, sy + j, n + 1
        end
    end
    if n > 0 then tm.camX, tm.camY = (sx / n + 0.5) * tm.size, (sy / n + 0.5) * tm.size end
end

-- the mouse wheel zooms the map about the cursor (the same limits as setTileMapScale)
local function wheelZoom()
    local c = env.cursor
    if not tm or not c or not c.wheelTriggered or not c.wheel or c.wheel == 0 then return end
    local sw, sh = screenSize()
    local wx, wy = screenToWorld(c.x, c.y)
    tm.scale = max(0.1, min(4, tm.scale * (c.wheel > 0 and 1.15 or 1 / 1.15)))
    local px, py = project(wx, wy)
    tm.camX, tm.camY = unproject(px - (c.x - sw * 0.5) / tm.scale, py - (c.y - sh * 0.5) / tm.scale)
    clampCamera()
end

function env.updateHatcheryMap(dt)
    wheelZoom()
    for _, o in pairs(objects) do
        for _, a in ipairs(o.anims) do
            local def = animations[a.id]
            local len = def and animationLength(def) or 0
            a.time = a.time + dt * a.speed
            if len > 0 then
                if a.loop then a.time = a.time % len elseif a.time > len then a.time = len end
            end
        end
    end
end

local function baseDef(ix, iy)
    if ix < 0 or iy < 0 or ix >= tm.w or iy >= tm.h then return nil end
    local gid = tm.base[iy * tm.w + ix + 1]
    if not gid or gid == 0 then return nil end
    return tm.defs[tostring(gid)], gid
end

function env.getStaticObjectID(wx, wy, layer)
    if not tm then return 0 end
    local ix, iy = floor(wx / tm.size), floor(wy / tm.size)
    if ix < 0 or iy < 0 or ix >= tm.w or iy >= tm.h then return 0 end
    return tm.base[iy * tm.w + ix + 1] or 0
end

local function inScreen(x, y, pad)
    local sw, sh = screenSize()
    return x > -pad and x < sw + pad and y > -pad and y < sh + pad
end

-- one object at a world position: every sprite is moved, scaled and turned by the object's animations, each about its own anchor
local function drawObject(o, wx, wy)
    local x, y = worldToScreen(wx, wy)
    if not inScreen(x, y, 500) then return end
    local k = tm.scale
    local count = #o.sprites
    for index, s in ipairs(o.sprites) do
        -- what the object holds (an egg, a bird) sits between the nest's back and its front rim, the last sprite
        if index == count and index > 1 and #o.children > 0 then
            for _, c in ipairs(o.children) do drawObject(c, wx, wy) end
        end
        local w, h = res.getSpriteBounds("", s.name)
        local px, py = res.getSpritePivot("", s.name)
        -- the sprite's own place: a point p of the sprite (from its pivot) goes to (tx, ty) + turn(angle) * scale * p
        local a, d, rot, tx, ty = s.sx, s.sy, s.angle or 0, s.ox, s.oy
        for _, an in ipairs(o.anims) do
            local def = animations[an.id]
            if def then
                local fx, fy, fsx, fsy, fr = sampleAnimation(def, an.time)
                local anchor = def.anchor
                local ax = (anchor and anchor[1] or 0.5) * w - px
                local ay = (anchor and anchor[2] or 0.5) * h - py
                local dx, dy = (tx - ax) * fsx, (ty - ay) * fsy
                local c, sn = cos(fr), sin(fr)
                tx = ax + c * dx - sn * dy + fx
                ty = ay + sn * dx + c * dy - fy
                a, d, rot = a * fsx, d * fsy, rot + fr
            end
        end
        blit(s.name, x + k * tx, y + k * ty, k * a, k * d, rot, 1)
    end
    if count <= 1 then for _, c in ipairs(o.children) do drawObject(c, wx, wy) end end
end

-- the tile art is drawn a little larger when the map is scaled, so no seams open between tiles
function env.drawHatcheryMap()
    if not tm then return end
    local sw, sh = screenSize()
    -- base tiles, back to front along the diagonal; only the visible window of the grid
    local x0, y0 = screenToWorld(-200, -200)
    local x1, y1 = screenToWorld(sw + 200, -200)
    local x2, y2 = screenToWorld(-200, sh + 200)
    local x3, y3 = screenToWorld(sw + 200, sh + 200)
    local s = tm.size
    local minI = max(0, floor(min(x0, x1, x2, x3) / s) - 1)
    local maxI = min(tm.w - 1, floor(max(x0, x1, x2, x3) / s) + 1)
    local minJ = max(0, floor(min(y0, y1, y2, y3) / s) - 1)
    local maxJ = min(tm.h - 1, floor(max(y0, y1, y2, y3) / s) + 1)
    local k = tm.scale
    local tileScale = (k == 1) and 1 or k * 1.012
    for sum = minI + minJ, maxI + maxJ do
        for i = max(minI, sum - maxJ), min(maxI, sum - minJ) do
            local j = sum - i
            local def = baseDef(i, j)
            local name = def and def.sprites and def.sprites[1]
            if name then
                local x, y = worldToScreen((i + 0.5) * s, (j + 0.5) * s)
                blit(name, x, y, tileScale, tileScale, 0, 1)
            end
        end
    end
    -- decorations and objects share one depth sort (the render queue first)
    local list = {}
    for _, d in ipairs(tm.decorations) do
        local x, y = worldToScreen(d.wx, d.wy)
        if inScreen(x, y, 400) then list[#list + 1] = { queue = d.queue, depth = d.depth, deco = d, x = x, y = y } end
    end
    for _, o in ipairs(placed) do
        list[#list + 1] = { queue = o.renderQueue or 0, depth = o.worldX + o.worldY, obj = o }
    end
    table.sort(list, function(a, b)
        if a.queue ~= b.queue then return a.queue < b.queue end
        return a.depth < b.depth
    end)
    for _, e in ipairs(list) do
        if e.deco then blit(e.deco.name, e.x, e.y, k, k, 0, 1)
        else drawObject(e.obj, e.obj.worldX, e.obj.worldY) end
    end
end

-- an object drawn once at a world position without being placed (the object being moved)
function env.drawTileObjectToWorld(id, wx, wy)
    local o = objects[id]
    if o and tm then drawObject(o, wx, wy) end
end

-- the tiles an object covers, drawn with an indicator sprite (green: it can be dropped here, red: it cannot)
function env.drawIndicatorForObject(id, wx, wy, sprite)
    local o = objects[id]
    if not o or not tm or not sprite then return end
    local s, k = tm.size, tm.scale
    local i0, j0, i1, j1 = footprint(o, wx, wy)
    for j = j0, j1 do
        for i = i0, i1 do
            local x, y = worldToScreen((i + 0.5) * s, (j + 0.5) * s)
            blit(sprite, x, y, k, k, 0, 1)
        end
    end
end

-- a screen-space sprite hung over a world location; ratioX/ratioY crop the sprite for progress bars
function env.drawHUDSpriteToTileWorldLocation(wx, wy, name, ratioX, ratioY)
    if not tm then return end
    local x, y = worldToScreen(wx, wy)
    ratioX = ratioX or 1
    ratioY = ratioY or 1
    if ratioX < 1 or ratioY < 1 then
        local w, h = res.getSpriteBounds("", name)
        local px, py = res.getSpritePivot("", name)
        res.setClipRect(x - px, y - py, w * ratioX, h * ratioY)
        res.drawSprite("", name, x, y)
        local sw, sh = screenSize()
        res.setClipRect(0, 0, sw, sh)
    else
        res.drawSprite("", name, x, y)
    end
end

-- ---- selection and placement ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- the rectangle on the screen an object covers (all its sprites)
local function screenRect(o, wx, wy)
    local x, y = worldToScreen(wx, wy)
    local k = tm.scale
    local l, t, r, b
    for _, s in ipairs(o.sprites) do
        local w, h = res.getSpriteBounds("", s.name)
        local px, py = res.getSpritePivot("", s.name)
        if w and w > 0 then
            local left = x + k * (s.ox - px * s.sx)
            local top = y + k * (s.oy - py * s.sy)
            local right, bottom = left + k * w * s.sx, top + k * h * s.sy
            if left > right then left, right = right, left end
            if top > bottom then top, bottom = bottom, top end
            l, t, r, b = min(l or left, left), min(t or top, top), max(r or right, right), max(b or bottom, bottom)
        end
    end
    return l, t, r, b
end

local function hitTest(o, wx, wy, cx, cy)
    local l, t, r, b = screenRect(o, wx, wy)
    if not l then return false end
    -- a child (egg, bird) in a nest counts as part of it
    for _, c in ipairs(o.children) do
        local cl, ct, cr, cb = screenRect(c, wx, wy)
        if cl then l, t, r, b = min(l, cl), min(t, ct), max(r, cr), max(b, cb) end
    end
    return cx >= l and cx <= r and cy >= t and cy <= b
end

function env.doesCursorIntersectTileObject(id, wx, wy, cx, cy)
    local o = objects[id]
    if not o or not tm then return false end
    if not cx then local c = env.cursor; cx, cy = c and c.x or 0, c and c.y or 0 end
    return hitTest(o, wx or o.worldX, wy or o.worldY, cx, cy)
end

function env.selectObjectVisibleAtPixel(x, y)
    local best, bestQ, bestD
    for _, o in ipairs(placed) do
        if o.selectable == true and hitTest(o, o.worldX, o.worldY, x, y) then
            local q, d = o.renderQueue or 0, o.worldX + o.worldY
            if not best or q > bestQ or (q == bestQ and d > bestD) then best, bestQ, bestD = o, q, d end
        end
    end
    if not best then return -1, 0, 0 end
    return best.id, best.worldX, best.worldY
end

local function tileOf(wx, wy) return floor(wx / tm.size), floor(wy / tm.size) end

local function covers(o, i, j)
    local i0, j0, i1, j1 = footprint(o, o.worldX, o.worldY)
    return i >= i0 and i <= i1 and j >= j0 and j <= j1
end

function env.selectTileObjectAtLocation(wx, wy)
    local i, j = tileOf(wx, wy)
    local best, bestQ
    for _, o in ipairs(placed) do
        if o.selectable == true and covers(o, i, j) and (not best or (o.renderQueue or 0) >= bestQ) then best, bestQ = o, o.renderQueue or 0 end
    end
    return best and best.id or -1
end

-- the object of the given type whose area contains the location (an egg needs an empty nest below it)
function env.getObjectOfType(wx, wy, t)
    local i, j = tileOf(wx, wy)
    for _, o in ipairs(placed) do
        if o.type == t and covers(o, i, j) then return o.id end
    end
    return -1
end

-- the area the object would take at (x, y) is on the map, on ground that can be built on, and free of other solid objects
function env.isObjectAreaFree(id, x, y)
    local o = objects[id]
    if not o or not tm then return false end
    local wx, wy = snapPosition(o, x, y)
    local i0, j0, i1, j1 = footprint(o, wx, wy)
    for j = j0, j1 do
        for i = i0, i1 do
            if i < 0 or j < 0 or i >= tm.w or j >= tm.h then return false end
            local def = baseDef(i, j)
            if not def or def.collision == true then return false end
            if tm.blocked[j * tm.w + i + 1] then return false end
        end
    end
    for _, other in ipairs(placed) do
        if other ~= o and other.collision == true then
            local a0, b0, a1, b1 = footprint(other, other.worldX, other.worldY)
            if not (a1 < i0 or a0 > i1 or b1 < j0 or b0 > j1) then return false end
        end
    end
    return true
end

-- ---- composite birds ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- drawCompoObjectLua(x, y, angle, scale, items): items = { {sprite, x, y, scale, angle}, ... } laid out about (x, y) in screen space
function env.drawCompoObjectLua(x, y, angle, scale, items)
    angle, scale = angle or 0, scale or 1
    local c, s = cos(angle), sin(angle)
    for _, it in ipairs(items or {}) do
        local ix, iy = (it.x or 0) * scale, (it.y or 0) * scale
        local sc = scale * (it.scale or 1)
        blit(it.sprite, x + c * ix - s * iy, y + s * ix + c * iy, sc, sc, angle + (it.angle or 0), 1)
    end
end

-- ---- misc natives the Hatchery calls ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- (the egg painter canvas, loadPersistentFileWrapper and checkForPersistentFile are in the engine)
function env.startAnalyzingCanvasColors() end
function env.stopAnalyzingCanvasColors() end
function env.drawHatcheryBackground() end
```

`src/lua/joint_page.lua`:

```lua
-- The level editor's joint window for the 1.6.x games that make the 1.6.0 joints (motor, limits, anchors) but ship no joint window
-- of their own (Angry Birds 1.6.2: Shift+J only made a plain distance joint). The window is the one of Angry Birds Seasons 2.3.0
-- (menus/item.lua, page.lua, overlayPage.lua and editorjointPage.lua, built into the engine, see lua_api.cpp). They run in a table
-- of their own, so Seasons' Page, TextItem and the other menu classes do not replace the game's; only EditorJointPage is handed over.
-- The engine runs this file among the game's globals when EditorJointPage is missing (script_host.cpp, EnsureClassicEditor).
local env = _G.getfenv(1)
-- while the files load, their classes stay in this table; afterwards a global the window sets (selectedObjects, levelSaved) is the game's
local loading = true
local own = _G.setmetatable({}, {__index = env, __newindex = function(t, k, v) if loading then _G.rawset(t, k, v) else env[k] = v end end})
own.this = own
-- `gamelua` for these files: Seasons' menu classes first (the window asks for gamelua.RectItem ...), then the game's globals
own.gamelua = _G.setmetatable({}, {__index = function(t, k) local v = _G.rawget(own, k) if v ~= nil then return v end return env[k] end, __newindex = env})
local function load(name) loadLuaFileToObject(scriptPath .. "/menus/" .. name, own, "") end
load("item.lua")
load("page.lua")
_G.rawset(own.gamelua, "page", {Page = own.Page})
load("editorjointPage.lua")
loading = false
EditorJointPage = own.EditorJointPage
```

```cpp
int l_print(lua_State* L) {
    std::string out;
    int n = lua_gettop(L);
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        if (i > 1) out += "\t";
        if (lua_isstring(L, i)) out += lua_tostring(L, i);
        else if (lua_isboolean(L, i)) out += lua_toboolean(L, i) ? "true" : "false";
        else out += luaL_typename(L, i);
    }

    return 0;

// createThemeSprite(name, sprite, x, y, scaleX, scaleY, angle, speedX, layer) and friends

int l_createThemeSprite(lua_State* L) {
    if (!RioMode(L) && IsSpaceData(L)) {
        P(L)->CreateThemeSpriteSpace(S(L, 1), S(L, 2), N(L, 3), N(L, 4), N(L, 5), N(L, 6), N(L, 7), (int)N(L, 8), N(L, 9), B(L, 10), lua_isnumber(L, 11) ? (float)lua_tonumber(L, 11) : 0.0f, lua_isnumber(L, 12) ? (float)lua_tonumber(L, 12) : 0.0f);
        return 0;
    }
    if (RioMode(L) || IsSpaceData(L)) {      // Rio and Space: ..., angle, layer, angleVel (Space calls it scaleSpeed), flipped [, velX, velY in Space]
        P(L)->CreateThemeSpriteRio(S(L, 1), S(L, 2), N(L, 3), N(L, 4), N(L, 5), N(L, 6), N(L, 7), (int)N(L, 8), N(L, 9), B(L, 10));
        return 0;
    }
    P(L)->CreateThemeSprite(S(L, 1), S(L, 2), N(L, 3), N(L, 4), N(L, 5), N(L, 6), N(L, 7), N(L, 8), (int)N(L, 9));
    return 0;
}
// createThemeAnimation(table) (0x484cc0): layer, x, y, scaleX, scaleY, angle, name, spriteName, velX, velY, scaleSpeed, startAnimTimer, animDelay,
// startingDelay, isAnimation, bLoop and animation (a list of the frames' sprite names)
int l_createThemeAnimation(lua_State* L) {
    if (!lua_istable(L, 1)) return 0;
    Platform::ThemeAnimation a;
    a.layer = (int)NumOr(L, 1, "layer", 0); a.x = NumOr(L, 1, "x", 0); a.y = NumOr(L, 1, "y", 0);
    a.scaleX = NumOr(L, 1, "scaleX", 1); a.scaleY = NumOr(L, 1, "scaleY", 1); a.angle = NumOr(L, 1, "angle", 0);
    if (Has(L, 1, "name")) a.name = FieldS(L, 1, "name");
    if (Has(L, 1, "spriteName")) a.sprite = FieldS(L, 1, "spriteName");
    a.velX = NumOr(L, 1, "velX", 0); a.velY = NumOr(L, 1, "velY", 0); a.scaleSpeed = NumOr(L, 1, "scaleSpeed", 0);
    a.animTimer = NumOr(L, 1, "startAnimTimer", 0);
    a.animDelay = NumOr(L, 1, "animDelay", 0);
    a.startingDelay = HasNum(L, 1, "startingDelay") ? FieldN(L, 1, "startingDelay") : a.animDelay;   // 0x484fe5: the delay starts as animDelay unless given
    a.loop = BoolOr(L, 1, "bLoop", false);
    lua_getfield(L, 1, "animation");
    if (lua_istable(L, -1))
        for (int i = 1;; i++) {
            lua_rawgeti(L, -1, i);
            if (!lua_isstring(L, -1)) { lua_pop(L, 1); break; }
            a.frames.push_back(lua_tostring(L, -1));
            lua_pop(L, 1);
        }
    lua_pop(L, 1);
    P(L)->CreateThemeAnimation(a);
    return 0;
}
int l_modifyThemeSprite(lua_State* L) {
    P(L)->ModifyThemeSprite(S(L, 1), N(L, 2), N(L, 3), N(L, 4), N(L, 5), N(L, 6), (int)N(L, 7));
    return 0;
}
int l_removeThemeSprite(lua_State* L) { P(L)->RemoveThemeSprite(S(L, 1), (int)N(L, 2)); return 0; }
int l_updateThemeSprite(lua_State* L) { P(L)->UpdateThemeSprites(N(L, 1)); return 0; }
int l_setThemeSprite(lua_State* L) { P(L)->SetThemeSprite(S(L, 1), S(L, 2), (int)N(L, 3)); return 0; }
int l_rotateThemeSprites(lua_State* L) { P(L)->RotateThemeSprites(N(L, 1)); return 0; }
int l_updateBackgroundAndForegroundScrollingNative(lua_State* L) { P(L)->ScrollThemeLayers(N(L, 1), B(L, 2)); return 0; }

// Seasons: loadLevelFile(path, date) asked a server for a level of that date and getLoadStatus() reported
// {status = ...} until the answer came. Levels are local here, so the answer is ready at once (status 1).
int l_getLoadStatus(lua_State* L) {
    lua_newtable(L);
    lua_pushnumber(L, 1);
    lua_setfield(L, -2, "status");
    return 1;
}

int l_throwException(lua_State* L) { P(L)->Print("script exception: " + S(L, 1)); return 0; }

// requireFile(name): Seasons 4.x. Runs script file `name` once (a second call with the same name does nothing), looked up in the game's script folder
// first and then in the common one (config.lua scriptPath / commonScriptPath); the file runs in the script environment like the main scripts.
int l_requireFile(lua_State* L) {
    const std::string name = S(L, 1);
    lua_getfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, "ab.required");
    if (!lua_istable(L, -1)) { lua_pop(L, 1); lua_newtable(L); lua_pushvalue(L, -1); lua_setfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, "ab.required"); }
    lua_getfield(L, -1, name.c_str());
    if (lua_toboolean(L, -1)) return 0;
    lua_pop(L, 1);
    lua_pushboolean(L, 1); lua_setfield(L, -2, name.c_str());
    lua_pop(L, 1);
    lua_getfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, "ab.env");
    std::string dirs[2];
    lua_getfield(L, -1, "scriptPath");       if (lua_isstring(L, -1)) dirs[0] = lua_tostring(L, -1); lua_pop(L, 1);
    lua_getfield(L, -1, "commonScriptPath"); if (lua_isstring(L, -1)) dirs[1] = lua_tostring(L, -1); lua_pop(L, 1);
    lua_pop(L, 1);
    std::vector<uint8_t> bytes;
    std::string path;
    for (const std::string& d : dirs) {
        if (d.empty()) continue;
        path = d + "/" + name;
        if (ab::ReadLuaFile(path, bytes) && !bytes.empty()) break;
        bytes.clear();
    }
    if (bytes.empty()) return luaL_error(L, "requireFile: cannot find %s", name.c_str());
    if (luaL_loadbuffer(L, (const char*)bytes.data(), bytes.size(), ("@" + path).c_str()) != 0) return lua_error(L);
    // v3.1: on the phone the game's globals are Lua's own, and Seasons 4.1.0 reads what these files make as _G.name (`Scaling = _G.Scaling`,
    // _G.platform.Profiles): every global a required file adds is put in the real global table too
    lua_getfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, "ab.env");
    int env = lua_gettop(L);
    lua_newtable(L);                                   // the names there were before
    int before = lua_gettop(L);
    lua_pushnil(L);
    while (lua_next(L, env)) { lua_pop(L, 1); lua_pushvalue(L, -1); lua_pushboolean(L, 1); lua_rawset(L, before); }
    lua_pushvalue(L, env);
    lua_setfenv(L, before - 2);                        // the chunk is below the two tables
    lua_pushvalue(L, before - 2);
    lua_call(L, 0, 0);
    lua_pushnil(L);
    while (lua_next(L, env)) {
        lua_pushvalue(L, -2); lua_rawget(L, before);
        bool old = !lua_isnil(L, -1);
        lua_pop(L, 1);
        if (!old && lua_type(L, -2) == LUA_TSTRING) {
            lua_pushvalue(L, -2); lua_rawget(L, LUA_GLOBALSINDEX);
            bool taken = !lua_isnil(L, -1);
            lua_pop(L, 1);
            if (!taken) { lua_pushvalue(L, -2); lua_pushvalue(L, -2); lua_rawset(L, LUA_GLOBALSINDEX); }
        }
        lua_pop(L, 1);
    }
    lua_pop(L, 3);
    return 0;
}

// v3.1: Angry Birds Friends 2.0.0 (the newer Rovio framework) loads its files through the `native` table:
// native.loadLuaTable(path [, ...]) runs a data file (an asset load list, a level) in a fresh table and returns that table,
// or nil and the error; native.loadLuaScript(name) runs a script from the script folder like requireFile and returns nil,
// or the error as a string (the game's own requireFile asserts on it).
int l_nativeLoadLuaTable(lua_State* L) {
    const std::string path = S(L, 1);
    std::vector<uint8_t> bytes;
    bool found = ab::ReadLuaFile(path, bytes) && !bytes.empty();
    std::string used = path;
    if (!found) { used = P(L)->ResolveDataFile(path); if (used != path) found = ab::ReadLuaFile(used, bytes) && !bytes.empty(); }
    if (!found) { lua_pushnil(L); lua_pushstring(L, ("cannot open " + path).c_str()); return 2; }
    if (luaL_loadbuffer(L, (const char*)bytes.data(), bytes.size(), ("@" + used).c_str()) != 0) { lua_pushnil(L); lua_insert(L, -2); return 2; }
    lua_newtable(L);                       // the file's globals land here; it can still read the game's (math, string ...)
    lua_newtable(L);
    lua_getfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, "ab.env");
    lua_setfield(L, -2, "__index");
    lua_setmetatable(L, -2);
    lua_pushvalue(L, -1);
    lua_setfenv(L, -3);
    lua_insert(L, -2);                     // table below the function
    if (lua_pcall(L, 0, 0, 0) != 0) { lua_pushnil(L); lua_insert(L, -2); return 2; }
    lua_pushnil(L);                        // a plain table for the game (pairs over it skips nothing)
    lua_setmetatable(L, -2);
    return 1;
}
int l_requireFile(lua_State* L);
// abListFolder(path) -> the names in a folder (folders end in "/"), for the Friends 2.0.0 stand-in server's tournament levels
// v3.1: abReadJson(path): a JSON file of the game's data (encrypted like the scripts or plain) as a Lua table, nil when it cannot be read.
// Angry Birds Stella keeps its Flash animations (.anim.json) and their skins (.skins.json) this way.
namespace {
struct JsonToLua {
    lua_State* L; const char* p; const char* e;
    void ws() { while (p < e && (*p == ' ' || *p == '\t' || *p == '\n' || *p == '\r')) p++; }
    bool str() {
        if (p >= e || *p != '"') return false;
        p++;
        std::string out;
        while (p < e && *p != '"') {
            if (*p == '\\' && p + 1 < e) {
                p++;
                char c = *p++;
                if (c == 'n') out += '\n'; else if (c == 't') out += '\t'; else if (c == 'r') out += '\r'; else if (c == 'b') out += '\b'; else if (c == 'f') out += '\f';
                else if (c == 'u' && p + 4 <= e) {
                    unsigned v = (unsigned)std::strtoul(std::string(p, 4).c_str(), nullptr, 16); p += 4;
                    if (v < 0x80) out += (char)v; else if (v < 0x800) { out += (char)(0xC0 | (v >> 6)); out += (char)(0x80 | (v & 0x3F)); }
                    else { out += (char)(0xE0 | (v >> 12)); out += (char)(0x80 | ((v >> 6) & 0x3F)); out += (char)(0x80 | (v & 0x3F)); }
                } else out += c;
            } else out += *p++;
        }
        if (p < e) p++;
        lua_pushlstring(L, out.data(), out.size());
        return true;
    }
    bool value(int depth) {
        ws();
        if (p >= e || depth > 200) return false;
        lua_checkstack(L, 4);
        if (*p == '{') {
            p++; lua_newtable(L); ws();
            if (p < e && *p == '}') { p++; return true; }
            while (p < e) {
                ws(); if (!str()) return false;
                ws(); if (p >= e || *p != ':') return false; p++;
                if (!value(depth + 1)) return false;
                lua_rawset(L, -3);
                ws(); if (p < e && *p == ',') { p++; continue; }
                if (p < e && *p == '}') { p++; return true; }
                return false;
            }
            return false;
        }
        if (*p == '[') {
            p++; lua_newtable(L); ws();
            int i = 1;
            if (p < e && *p == ']') { p++; return true; }
            while (p < e) {
                if (!value(depth + 1)) return false;
                lua_rawseti(L, -2, i++);
                ws(); if (p < e && *p == ',') { p++; continue; }
                if (p < e && *p == ']') { p++; return true; }
                return false;
            }
            return false;
        }
        if (*p == '"') return str();
        if (e - p >= 4 && std::strncmp(p, "true", 4) == 0) { p += 4; lua_pushboolean(L, 1); return true; }
        if (e - p >= 5 && std::strncmp(p, "false", 5) == 0) { p += 5; lua_pushboolean(L, 0); return true; }
        if (e - p >= 4 && std::strncmp(p, "null", 4) == 0) { p += 4; lua_pushboolean(L, 0); return true; }   // (a nil cannot be a table value)
        char* end = nullptr;
        double d = std::strtod(p, &end);
        if (end == p) return false;
        p = end; lua_pushnumber(L, d);
        return true;
    }
};
}  // namespace

int l_abReadJson(lua_State* L) {
    std::string file = S(L, 1);
    std::vector<uint8_t> bytes;
    ab::ReadLuaFile(P(L)->ResolveDataFile(file), bytes);
    if (bytes.empty()) { lua_pushnil(L); return 1; }
    int top = lua_gettop(L);
    JsonToLua j{L, (const char*)bytes.data(), (const char*)bytes.data() + bytes.size()};
    if (!j.value(0)) { lua_settop(L, top); P(L)->Print("abReadJson: could not read " + file); lua_pushnil(L); return 1; }
    return 1;
}

int l_abListFolder(lua_State* L) {
    std::vector<std::string> names = ab::ListFolder(S(L, 1));
    lua_newtable(L);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < names.size(); i++) { lua_pushstring(L, names[i].c_str()); lua_rawseti(L, -2, (int)i + 1); }
    return 1;
}
int l_nativeLoadLuaScript(lua_State* L) {
    lua_pushcfunction(L, l_requireFile);
    lua_pushvalue(L, 1);
    if (lua_pcall(L, 1, 0, 0) != 0) return 1;      // the error message
    return 0;
}

int l_loadLuaFileToObject(lua_State* L) {
    // loadLuaFileToObject(path, object, name): runs the file in a table of its own that falls back to
    // `object` for names it does not define, then stores that table as object[name]
    std::string path = S(L, 1);
    {   // v3.1: Seasons 4.1.0's dynamic assets need the phone's asset handler (createDynamicHandler): without it the game loads its images the usual way
        const char* dyn = "/dynamicassets.lua";
        size_t n = std::strlen(dyn);
        if (path.size() >= n && path.compare(path.size() - n, n, dyn) == 0) {
            PushEnv(L);
            lua_getfield(L, -1, "createDynamicHandler");
            bool none = lua_isnil(L, -1);
            lua_pop(L, 1);
            if (none) { lua_pushboolean(L, 0); lua_setfield(L, -2, "useDynamicAssets"); }
            lua_pop(L, 1);
            if (none) return 0;
        }
    }
    bool toObject = lua_istable(L, 2) && lua_isstring(L, 3);
    bool spaceBlocks = false;
    std::vector<uint8_t> bytes;
    int rc = 1;
    // Angry Birds Island HD (Hatchery) names its files from the data folder ("hatchery/scripts/..."); try that when the path does not exist as written
    bool found = ab::ReadLuaFile(path, bytes);
    if (!found) { std::string alt = P(L)->ResolveDataFile(path); if (alt != path) found = ab::ReadLuaFile(alt, bytes); }
    // the two ui components the Hatchery needs that 2.0.0's PC scripts do not have (CompoImage, InvisibleButton) are built in
    if (!found) {
        const struct { const char* file; const unsigned char* data; unsigned size; } builtIn[] = {
            {"ui_components/CompoImage.lua", kCompoImageLua, kCompoImageLuaSize},
            {"menus/editorjointPage.lua", kEditorJointPageLua, kEditorJointPageLuaSize},   // v3.1: Seasons 2.3.0's joint window, for the 1.6.x editors without one (joint_page.lua)
            {"menus/overlayPage.lua", kOverlayPageLua, kOverlayPageLuaSize},
            {"menus/page.lua", kPageLua, kPageLuaSize},
            {"menus/item.lua", kItemLua, kItemLuaSize},
            {"ui_components/InvisibleButton.lua", kInvisibleButtonLua, kInvisibleButtonLuaSize}};
        for (const auto& b : builtIn) {
            size_t n = std::strlen(b.file);
            if (path.size() >= n && path.compare(path.size() - n, n, b.file) == 0) { bytes.assign(b.data, b.data + b.size); found = true; }
        }
    }
    if (found) rc = luaL_loadbuffer(L, (const char*)bytes.data(), bytes.size(), ("@" + path).c_str());
    else lua_pushstring(L, ("cannot open " + path).c_str());
    if (rc == 0) {
        if (toObject) {
            if (*lua_tostring(L, 3) == 0) {
                lua_pushvalue(L, 2);                    // 2.0.0, name "": the file runs in the object itself
            } else {
                lua_newtable(L);                        // the file's table
                lua_newtable(L);                        // its metatable { __index = object }
                lua_pushvalue(L, 2);
                lua_setfield(L, -2, "__index");
                {   // v3.1: in Seasons 4.1.0 `this` is the object a file is loaded into (BlockScriptManager.lua loads BlockEvents.lua "into this" as
                    // `events`: falling back to the game's `this` replaced the game's own events table, and every level stopped at its first event)
                    PushEnv(L);
                    lua_getfield(L, -1, "abObjectThis");
                    const bool own = lua_toboolean(L, -1) != 0;
                    lua_pop(L, 2);
                    if (own) { lua_pushvalue(L, -2); lua_setfield(L, -3, "this"); }
                }
                if (std::strcmp(lua_tostring(L, 3), "Hatchery") == 0) {
                    // hatchery.lua loads the rest of the Hatchery (its UI files, ui components, events) "into this": for this file `this` is the
                    // file's own table, so everything it defines (hatchery, hatcheryEventManager, ui ...) is shared by those files and stays
                    // out of the game's globals
                    lua_pushvalue(L, -2);
                    lua_setfield(L, -3, "this");
                    // and the Hatchery is written for the iPad (its sheets, context menu and panels pick their layout from gamelua.deviceModel):
                    // its `gamelua` reads everything from the game's, except that the device is an iPad
                    luaL_loadstring(L, "local env = ...; return setmetatable({deviceModel = \"ipad\"}, {__index = env, __newindex = env})");
                    lua_pushvalue(L, 2);
                    lua_call(L, 1, 1);
                    lua_setfield(L, -3, "gamelua");
                }
                lua_setmetatable(L, -2);
                // an object without a metatable of its own falls back to the globals, so the menu files
                // (Angry Birds Rio) also find `gamelua`, `res` and the engine functions by bare name
                if (!lua_getmetatable(L, 2)) {
                    PushEnv(L);
                    if (!lua_rawequal(L, -1, 2)) {
                        lua_newtable(L);
                        lua_pushvalue(L, -2);
                        lua_setfield(L, -2, "__index");
                        lua_setmetatable(L, 2);
                    }
                    lua_pop(L, 1);
                } else lua_pop(L, 1);
                lua_pushvalue(L, -1);
                lua_setfield(L, 2, lua_tostring(L, 3)); // object[name] = the file's table
            }
            lua_setfenv(L, -2);
        } else if (lua_isstring(L, 2) && *lua_tostring(L, 2)) {
            // loadLuaFile(path, name): the file runs in a table of its own (names it does not define come from
            // the globals) and that table becomes the global `name`, e.g. cutscenes
            // Angry Birds Space loads each block file with loadLuaFile(path, "blockTable"): the definitions it lists are filed
            // under blockTable.blocks[definition] (as the Rio loader does); materials, damage factors, themes and groups also
            // become fields of blockTable
            const bool isBlocks = std::strcmp(lua_tostring(L, 2), "blockTable") == 0;
            PushEnv(L);                                 // the globals
            lua_newtable(L);                            // the file's table
            lua_newtable(L);
            lua_pushvalue(L, -3);
            lua_setfield(L, -2, "__index");
            lua_setmetatable(L, -2);
            if (!isBlocks) {
                lua_pushvalue(L, -1);
                lua_setfield(L, -3, lua_tostring(L, 2));    // globals[name] = the file's table
                static const char* kNested[] = {"materials", "damageFactors", "themes", "groups", "staticGroundCollisionSounds"};   // (the last: Stella reads blockTable.staticGroundCollisionSounds)
                for (const char* nn : kNested) if (std::strcmp(lua_tostring(L, 2), nn) == 0) {
                    lua_getfield(L, -2, "blockTable");
                    if (!lua_istable(L, -1)) {
                        lua_pop(L, 1);
                        lua_newtable(L);
                        lua_pushvalue(L, -1);
                        lua_setfield(L, -4, "blockTable");
                    }
                    lua_pushvalue(L, -2);
                    lua_setfield(L, -2, nn);
                    lua_pop(L, 1);
                }
            } else {
                lua_getfield(L, -2, "blockTable");
                if (!lua_istable(L, -1)) {
                    lua_pop(L, 1);
                    lua_newtable(L);
                    lua_pushvalue(L, -1);
                    lua_setfield(L, -4, "blockTable");
                }
                lua_getfield(L, -1, "blocks");
                if (!lua_istable(L, -1)) { lua_pop(L, 1); lua_newtable(L); lua_pushvalue(L, -1); lua_setfield(L, -3, "blocks"); }
                lua_pop(L, 2);
                // remember the file's table to file it after the run
                lua_pushvalue(L, -1);
                lua_setfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, "ab.blockfile");
            }
            lua_remove(L, -2);
            lua_setfenv(L, -2);
            spaceBlocks = isBlocks;
        } else {
            PushEnv(L);
            lua_setfenv(L, -2);
        }
        rc = lua_pcall(L, 0, 0, 0);
        if (rc == 0 && toObject && *lua_tostring(L, 3) == 0 && path.size() >= 10 && path.compare(path.size() - 10, 10, "themes.lua") == 0) {
            // v3.1: Star Wars 1.0 (iPhone) writes filename = "themes.lua" into the themes table, and its editor start (createAssets with showEditor)
            // walks every entry as a theme; the plain string is not a theme
            lua_getfield(L, 2, "filename");
            bool str = lua_type(L, -1) == LUA_TSTRING;
            lua_pop(L, 1);
            if (str) { lua_pushnil(L); lua_setfield(L, 2, "filename"); }
        }
        if (rc == 0 && spaceBlocks) {
            const char* filer =
                "local T, bt, env = ...\nlocal pairs, ipairs, type = _G.pairs, _G.ipairs, _G.type\n"
                "for k, v in pairs(T) do\n"
                "  if type(v) == 'number' then env[k] = v\n"
                "  elseif type(v) == 'table' then\n"
                "    for _, e in ipairs(v) do\n"
                "      if type(e) == 'table' and type(e.definition) == 'string' then bt.blocks[e.definition] = e end\n"
                "    end\n"
                "  end\n"
                "end\n"
                "if not bt.blocks.Ground then bt.blocks.Ground = {definition = 'Ground', type = 'box', sprite = '', texture = '', material = 'immovable'} end\n";
            if (luaL_loadstring(L, filer) == 0) {
                lua_getfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, "ab.blockfile");
                PushEnv(L);
                lua_getfield(L, -1, "blockTable");
                lua_insert(L, -2);                      // T, blockTable, env
                if (lua_pcall(L, 3, 0, 0) != 0) { P(L)->Print(std::string("blockTable: ") + lua_tostring(L, -1)); lua_pop(L, 1); }
            } else lua_pop(L, 1);
        }
        if (rc == 0) {
            // debug build: MainMenu.init / MainMenu.layout run with releaseBuild false (shows the 2.0.0 EDITOR button)
            lua_getfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, "ab.view");
            PushEnv(L);
            lua_getfield(L, -1, "MainMenu");
            if (lua_istable(L, -1) && lua_istable(L, -3)) {
                for (const char* name : {"init", "layout"}) {
                    lua_pushstring(L, name);
                    lua_rawget(L, -2);
                    if (lua_isfunction(L, -1)) { lua_pushvalue(L, -4); lua_setfenv(L, -2); }
                    lua_pop(L, 1);
                }
            }
            lua_pop(L, 3);
            // debug build: the iPad scripts keep the star coins and stars, and the Hatchery state, in settingsWrapper; 2.0.0's PC copy lacks them
            const std::string sw = "settingsWrapper.lua";
            if (!std::getenv("AB_NODEBUGKEYS") && path.size() >= sw.size() && path.compare(path.size() - sw.size(), sw.size(), sw) == 0) {
                const char* wrapper =
                    "local sw = settingsWrapper or SettingsWrapper\n"
                    "if sw == nil then return end\n"
                    "if sw.getAvailableStarCoins == nil then\n"
                    "    function sw:getAvailableStarCoins() return settings.starCoins or 1000 end\n"
                    "    function sw:setAvailableStarCoins(val) settings.starCoins = val end\n"
                    "    function sw:getAvailableStars() return settings.stars or 1000 end\n"
                    "    function sw:setAvailableStars(val) settings.stars = val end\n"
                    "end\n"
                    "for _, name in _G.ipairs({\"setHatcheryLocalTime\", \"setHatcheryState\", \"setHatcheryLastSavedServerTime\"}) do\n"
                    "    if sw[name] == nil then\n"
                    "        local key = \"hatchery\" .. _G.string.sub(name, 12)\n"
                    "        sw[name] = function(self, value) settings[key] = value end\n"
                    "    end\n"
                    "end\n";
                if (luaL_loadstring(L, wrapper) == 0) {

            }
            // debug build: this copy of hatchery.lua has the WORLD_VIEW link commented out in init, but enter() still goes there

                const char* link =

            }
            // debug build: the Hatchery's shop log is drawn for the iPad's 1024 pixel wide screen; on a wider window its buttons are centred on the log
            const std::string wsp = "hatchery/scripts/UI/WorldSelectionPanel.lua";

                    "    layout(self)\n"
                    "    self:getChild(\"purchaseButton\").x = gamelua.screenWidth * 0.5 - 512 + 0.08 * 1024\n"
                    "end\n";
                if (luaL_loadstring(L, shop) == 0) {
                    lua_pushvalue(L, 2);
                    lua_setfenv(L, -2);
                    if (lua_pcall(L, 0, 0, 0) != 0) { P(L)->Print(std::string("shop layout: ") + lua_tostring(L, -1)); lua_pop(L, 1); }
                } else { P(L)->Print(std::string("shop layout: ") + lua_tostring(L, -1)); lua_pop(L, 1); }
            }
            // debug build: the iPad's in-game bird selector hangs its button at the screen's corner with an iPad-only sprite; here it sits after the
            // pause button (and the restart button next to it) and is only there while the pause button is
            const std::string bs = "hatchery/scripts/UI/BirdSelector.lua";

                if (luaL_loadstring(L, selector) == 0) {

                    if (lua_pcall(L, 0, 0, 0) != 0) { P(L)->Print(std::string("bird selector: ") + lua_tostring(L, -1)); lua_pop(L, 1); }
                } else { P(L)->Print(std::string("bird selector: ") + lua_tostring(L, -1)); lua_pop(L, 1); }
            }
            // debug build: the iPad's ChallengePage.lua calls ChallengeFrame:storeViewedChallenges() on entry, but the function is inside a comment there
            const std::string cp = "challenges/ChallengePage.lua";
            if (!std::getenv("AB_NODEBUGKEYS") && path.size() >= cp.size() && path.compare(path.size() - cp.size(), cp.size(), cp) == 0) {
                const char* store = "if ChallengeFrame and ChallengeFrame.storeViewedChallenges == nil then function ChallengeFrame:storeViewedChallenges() end end\n";
                if (luaL_loadstring(L, store) == 0) {
                    PushEnv(L);
                    lua_setfenv(L, -2);
                    if (lua_pcall(L, 0, 0, 0) != 0) { P(L)->Print(std::string("challenge page: ") + lua_tostring(L, -1)); lua_pop(L, 1); }
                } else { P(L)->Print(std::string("challenge page: ") + lua_tostring(L, -1)); lua_pop(L, 1); }
            }
            // debug build: the Challenges badge and the Hatchery button of the episode selection are drawn with the iPad's (larger) sprites; they are
            // made smaller and moved apart so they do not overlap each other or the first episode
            const std::string es = "menus/episode_selection.lua";
            if (!std::getenv("AB_NODEBUGKEYS") && path.size() >= es.size() && path.compare(path.size() - es.size(), es.size(), es) == 0) {
                const char* episodes =
                    "local layout = EpisodeScrollFrame.layout\n"
                    "function EpisodeScrollFrame:layout()\n"

                    "    local challenge, hatchery = self:getChild(\"challengeButton\"), self:getChild(\"hatcheryButton\")\n"

                    lua_setfenv(L, -2);

                } else { P(L)->Print(std::string("episode selection: ") + lua_tostring(L, -1)); lua_pop(L, 1); }
            }
            // debug build: the buttons of the iPad's BuyStarsDialog are empty planks (the amounts were drawn by the App Store layer); the amounts are written on them
            const std::string bsd = "UI/BuyStarsDialog.lua";

                const char* amounts =
```
