`src/lua/space_editor.lua`:

```lua
-- Level editor for Angry Birds Space. The retail exe has the editor's natives (blockEditorTable, saveLevel, createObject ...) but no editor scripts,
-- so the engine brings this one. It wraps the game's own update() and draw(): F2 switches it on while a level is running, F2 again plays on.
-- Run once into the script environment by script_host.cpp (EnsureSpaceEditor); nothing happens until F2 is pressed.
local env = ...
local G = env._G

local editor = {
    active = false, selected = nil, dragging = false, dragDX = 0, dragDY = 0,
    palette = nil, index = 1, counter = 0, message = "", messageTime = 0, wasPhysics = true, saved = false,
}
env.spaceEditor = editor

local function say(text) editor.message = text; editor.messageTime = 3 end

local function buildPalette()
    local list = {}
    local blocks = env.blockTable and env.blockTable.blocks
    if blocks then
        for name, def in G.pairs(blocks) do
            if G.type(def) == "table" and def.sprite and not name:find("MENU") and not name:find("^BLOCK_COMIC") then list[#list + 1] = name end
        end
    end
    table.sort(list)
    editor.palette = list
    if editor.index > #list then editor.index = 1 end
end

-- how far from the centre of an object a click still hits it (physics units)
local function reach(obj)
    local def = env.blockTable and env.blockTable.blocks[obj.definition]
    if not def then return 1.5 end
    local r = def.radius or math.max(def.width or 0, def.height or 0) / 2
    if not r or r <= 0 then r = 1.5 end
    return r
end

local function pick(px, py)
    local best, bestR = nil, nil
    for name, obj in G.pairs(env.objects.world) do
        if G.type(obj) == "table" and obj.x and obj.y and obj.definition then
            local r = reach(obj)
            local d = math.sqrt((obj.x - px) ^ 2 + (obj.y - py) ^ 2)
            if d <= r + 1 and (bestR == nil or r < bestR) then best, bestR = name, r end
        end
    end
    return best
end

local function setActive(on)
    editor.active = on
    if on then
        editor.wasPhysics = env.isPhysicsEnabled and env.isPhysicsEnabled() or true
        env.setPhysicsEnabled(false)
        if not editor.palette then buildPalette() end
        say("Editor on: left drag moves, N places, Q/E turn, Delete removes, Ctrl+S saves")
    else
        env.setPhysicsEnabled(editor.wasPhysics ~= false)
        editor.selected, editor.dragging = nil, false
    end
end

local function editorUpdate(dt)
    local kp, kh = env.keyPressed, env.keyHold
    local px, py = env.screenToPhysicsTransform(env.cursor.x, env.cursor.y)
    if editor.messageTime > 0 then editor.messageTime = editor.messageTime - dt end

    -- camera: arrow keys pan, the wheel zooms
    local pan = 600 * dt
    local sx, sy = env.screen.x or 0, env.screen.y or 0
    local dx = (kh.RIGHT and pan or 0) - (kh.LEFT and pan or 0)
    local dy = (kh.DOWN and pan or 0) - (kh.UP and pan or 0)
    if dx ~= 0 or dy ~= 0 then env.setTopLeft(sx + dx, sy + dy) end
    if env.cursor.wheel and env.cursor.wheel ~= 0 and not kh.SHIFT then
        local ws = (env.worldScale or 1) * (env.cursor.wheel > 0 and 1.1 or 1 / 1.1)
        env.worldScale = ws
        env.setWorldScale(ws)
    end

    -- the palette: Shift + wheel, or PageUp / PageDown
    if (env.cursor.wheel and env.cursor.wheel ~= 0 and kh.SHIFT) or kp.PAGEUP or kp.PAGEDOWN then
        local step = (kp.PAGEDOWN or (env.cursor.wheel or 0) < 0) and 1 or -1
        editor.index = (editor.index - 1 + step) % #editor.palette + 1
        say("Block: " .. editor.palette[editor.index])
    end

    -- selection and dragging
    if kp.LBUTTON then
        editor.selected = pick(px, py)
        editor.dragging = editor.selected ~= nil
        if editor.selected then
            local o = env.objects.world[editor.selected]
            editor.dragDX, editor.dragDY = o.x - px, o.y - py
        end
    end
    if editor.dragging and kh.LBUTTON and editor.selected and env.objects.world[editor.selected] then
        env.setPosition(editor.selected, px + editor.dragDX, py + editor.dragDY)
        editor.saved = false
    elseif not kh.LBUTTON then
        editor.dragging = false
    end

    local sel = editor.selected and env.objects.world[editor.selected]
    if sel and (kp.Q or kp.E) then
        local a = (sel.angle or 0) + (kp.E and 1 or -1) * (kh.SHIFT and 0.0174533 or 0.0872665)
        env.setRotation(editor.selected, a)
        editor.saved = false
    end
    if sel and (kp.DELETE or kp.BACKSPACE) then
        env.destroyObject(editor.selected, true)
        editor.selected, editor.dragging = nil, false
        editor.saved = false
    end

    -- N places the chosen block at the cursor, D copies the selected one
    if kp.N or (kp.D and sel) then
        local def = kp.N and editor.palette[editor.index] or sel.definition
        editor.counter = editor.counter + 1
        local name = def .. "_ed" .. editor.counter
        while env.objects.world[name] do editor.counter = editor.counter + 1; name = def .. "_ed" .. editor.counter end
        local ok = env.createObject(env.blockTable, def, name, px, py, kp.D and sel.angle or 0)
        if ok ~= nil or env.objects.world[name] then editor.selected = name; editor.saved = false; say("Placed " .. name) end
    end

    if kh.CONTROL and kp.S then
        local path = (env.levelFolder or "levels/") .. (env.levelName or "Level")
        env.saveLevel(path)
        editor.saved = true
        say("Saved " .. path)
    end
    if kp.F2 then setActive(false) end
end

local function wrap()
    local gameUpdate, gameDraw = env.update, env.draw
    if G.type(gameUpdate) ~= "function" or G.type(gameDraw) ~= "function" or editor.wrapped then return end
    editor.wrapped = true
    env.update = function(dt, time)
        if editor.active then
            editorUpdate(dt)
            return
        end
        if env.keyPressed.F2 and env.objects and env.objects.world and env.blockTable and env.levelName and env.levelName ~= "MainMenu" then
            setActive(true)
            return
        end
        return gameUpdate(dt, time)
    end
    env.draw = function()
        gameDraw()
        if not editor.active then return end
        env.setFont(env.FONT_BASIC)
        env.setRenderState(0, 0, 1, 1, 0)
        local sel = editor.selected and env.objects.world[editor.selected]
        if sel then
            local sxp, syp = env.physicsToScreenTransform(sel.x, sel.y)
            local r = reach(sel) * 20 * (env.worldScale or 1)
            if r < 12 then r = 12 end
            env.drawRectLines(sxp - r, syp - r, sxp + r, syp + r, 2, 255, 220, 0, 255)
            env.res.drawString("", editor.selected, sxp, syp - r - 4, "BOTTOM", "HCENTER")
        end
        local def = editor.palette and editor.palette[editor.index] or "?"
        env.res.drawString("", "EDITOR  block: " .. def .. (editor.saved and "" or "  (unsaved)"), 8, 8, "TOP", "LEFT")
        if editor.messageTime > 0 then env.res.drawString("", editor.message, 8, 34, "TOP", "LEFT") end
    end
end
editor.install = wrap
wrap()

```

```lua
-- Angry Birds Space natives that are plain maths or logging; run once into the script environment (the C++ ones are in lua_api.cpp)
local env = ...
function env.performBitwiseOr(...)
    local r = 0
    for _, v in ipairs({...}) do
        local out, bit = 0, 1
        local a, b = r, v
        while a > 0 or b > 0 do
            if a % 2 == 1 or b % 2 == 1 then out = out + bit end
            a = math.floor(a / 2); b = math.floor(b / 2); bit = bit * 2
        end
        r = out
    end
    return r
end
function env.dotProduct(x1, y1, x2, y2) return x1 * x2 + y1 * y2 end
function env.normalizeVector(x, y)
    local l = math.sqrt(x * x + y * y)
    if l == 0 then return {x = 0, y = 0} end
    return {x = x / l, y = y / l}
end
function env.transformCoordinates(angle, x, y)
    local c, s = math.cos(angle), math.sin(angle)
    return {x = x * c - y * s, y = x * s + y * c}

-- (-45 degrees), `depth` runs along the plane (the line's yPosition: larger is nearer the viewer), and the line shrinks and fades towards the far end.
ifMissing("drawString3D", function(group, text, x, y, z, tilt, turn, depth, alpha)
    local w, h = env.screenWidth, env.screenHeight
    local c, sn = _G.math.cos(tilt), _G.math.sin(-tilt)
    local zz = z - depth * c
    if zz < 1 then return end
    local s = h * 0.55 / zz
    local a = _G.math.max(0, _G.math.min(1, alpha or 1))

    env.res.drawString(group, text, (w * 0.5 + x * s) / s, (h * 0.5 + (y + depth * sn) * s) / sy, "LEFT", "VCENTER")
    env.setRenderState(0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1)
end)


-- renderGravityVisualsNative(sensor, screenX, screenY, zoom) (0x415f90): the rings (circle sensors) and bars (box sensors) that the script's gravityVisuals list
-- keeps for a gravitation sensor. A circle entry's sprite is drawn eight times round the sensor (four turns of a quarter, then four more shifted by an eighth),
-- scaled by entry.scale * radius * 3 * zoom * 0.019; a box entry's sprite is drawn along the sensor's length at entry.pos (0..1), turned a quarter past the sensor's angle.
-- (The game's own script passes no zoom, which reads as 0 in the exe, so the retail game draws nothing; a mod that passes the zoom gets the rings.)
-- Every circle sprite is turned about its own pivot (which lies outside the slice, at the field's centre) and drawn with the pivot anchors (VPIVOT, HPIVOT).
ifMissing("renderGravityVisualsNative", function(sen, sx, sy, zoom)
    zoom = zoom or 0   -- the retail script passes only three arguments, and the exe's number reader gives 0 for the missing fourth: scaled to nothing, so nothing is drawn
    if type(sen) ~= "table" or sen.sensorType == nil or sen.addVisualTimer == nil or not sen.active or sen.definition == nil then return end
    local def = env.blockTable and env.blockTable.blocks and env.blockTable.blocks[sen.definition]
    local vis = sen.gravityVisuals
    if not def or type(vis) ~= "table" then return end
    local pi = _G.math.pi
    if def.type == "circle" then
        local unit = (sen.radius or 0) * 3.0 * zoom * 0.019
        for _, e in _G.ipairs(vis) do
            local s = (e.scale or 1) * unit
            if s ~= 0 then
                local w, h = env.res.getSpritePivot(e.sprite)   -- 1.1.0 0xe5de / 0xe5f0 read the sprite's pivot (+0x14 / +0x16): the slice's pivot is the field's centre
                for pass = 0, 1 do
                    for i = 1, 4 do
                        env.setRenderState(sx / s, sy / s, s, s, (i - 1) * pi * 0.5 + pass * pi * 0.25, w, h)
                        env.res.drawSprite(e.sprite, e.x or 0, e.y or 0, "VPIVOT", "HPIVOT")
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    elseif def.type == "box" and sen.width and sen.height then
        local hw, hh = sen.width * 20 * 0.5, sen.height * 20 * 0.5
        local pw, ph = env.res.getSpriteBounds("THEME_1_GRAVITY_SLICE_BOX_FADED")
        if not pw or pw == 0 then return end
        local u = hw * 2 / pw
        local a = sen.angle or 0
        local cs, sn = _G.math.cos(a), _G.math.sin(a)
        local s = u * zoom
        if s == 0 then return end
        env.setRenderState(sx / s, sy / s, s, s, pi * 0.5 + a, pw, ph)
        for _, e in _G.ipairs(vis) do
            local p = e.pos or 0
            env.res.drawSprite(e.sprite, (p * 2 * hh * sn - hh * sn) / u, (-p * 2 * hh * cs + hh * cs) / u, "VPIVOT", "HPIVOT")
        end
    end
end)

-- the setters of single flags on the object record (0x4290d0, 0x428290, 0x428050, 0x427fe0, 0x427f70, 0x427e90, 0x427f00, 0x4280c0): the object record
-- keeps them, 200 and up are the engine's own setObjectParameter ids
local function flagNative(nativeName, id)

-- res.createCompositeAudio(name, {clip names}): a sound made of other sounds that play one after the other
-- (Star Wars: the title theme, then the menu music). Without it startInitialLoading failed in createAudioAssets and restarted every frame.
if env.res and env.res.createCompositeAudio == nil and env.res.playAudio then
    local res, composites, running = env.res, {}, {}
    local playAudio, stopAudio, stopAll = res.playAudio, res.stopAudio, res.stopAllAudio
    res.createCompositeAudio = function(name, clips) composites[name] = clips end
    res.playAudio = function(name, ...)
        local clips = composites[name]
        if not clips then return playAudio(name, ...) end
        running[name] = {index = 1, args = {...}}
        return playAudio(clips[1], ...)
    end
    res.stopAudio = function(name, ...)
        local clips = composites[name]
        if clips then running[name] = nil; for _, c in ipairs(clips) do stopAudio(c, ...) end return end
        return stopAudio(name, ...)
    end
    if stopAll then res.stopAllAudio = function(...) running = {} return stopAll(...) end end
    local isPlaying = res.isAudioPlaying
    if isPlaying then
        res.isAudioPlaying = function(name, ...)
            if composites[name] then return running[name] ~= nil end
            return isPlaying(name, ...)
        end
    end
    -- the next clip of every running composite starts when the one before it has ended
    local update = env.update
    env.update = function(...)
        for name, run in pairs(running) do
            local clips = composites[name]
            if not isPlaying(clips[run.index]) then
                run.index = run.index + 1
                if clips[run.index] then playAudio(clips[run.index], unpack(run.args)) else running[name] = nil end
            end
        end
        return update(...)
    end
end

-- ---- Star Wars cutscenes: the "game::Animation" files (encrypted JSON) of the menus and the power-up tutorials
-- cutsceneLoad(tag, file), cutsceneStart(tag, action, mode "once" / "repeat"), cutsceneSetTranslation / Scale / Rotation(tag, ...), updateCutscene(dt),
-- drawCutscene(tag), cutsceneClose(tag). A clip is a list of targets named <parent>_<parent layer>_<name>_L<layer>; each target animates a translation,
-- scale, rotation and the sprite shown. Layer 0 is on top (Flash), and the children of a target are drawn over it.
if env.readDataFile then
    local cuts = {}
    local function parseJson(text)
        local pos = 1
        local function skip() pos = text:find("[^ \t\r\n]", pos) or #text + 1 end
        local value
        local function str()
            local out, i = {}, pos + 1
            while true do
                local c = text:sub(i, i)
                if c == '"' then pos = i + 1 return table.concat(out) end
                if c == "\\" then
                    local n = text:sub(i + 1, i + 1)
                    out[#out + 1] = ({n = "\n", t = "\t", r = "\r"})[n] or n
                    i = i + 2
                else out[#out + 1] = c i = i + 1 end
            end
        end
        function value()
            skip()
            local c = text:sub(pos, pos)
            if c == "{" then
                local t, order = {}, {}
                pos = pos + 1 skip()
                if text:sub(pos, pos) == "}" then pos = pos + 1 t.__order = order return t end
                while true do
                    skip()
                    local k = str() skip()
                    pos = pos + 1   -- the colon
                    t[k] = value() order[#order + 1] = k skip()
                    local d = text:sub(pos, pos) pos = pos + 1
                    if d == "}" then break end
                end
                t.__order = order
                return t
            elseif c == "[" then
                local t = {}
                pos = pos + 1 skip()
                if text:sub(pos, pos) == "]" then pos = pos + 1 return t end
                while true do
                    t[#t + 1] = value() skip()
                    local d = text:sub(pos, pos) pos = pos + 1
                    if d == "]" then break end
                end
                return t
            elseif c == '"' then return str()
            elseif text:sub(pos, pos + 3) == "true" then pos = pos + 4 return true
            elseif text:sub(pos, pos + 4) == "false" then pos = pos + 5 return false
            elseif text:sub(pos, pos + 3) == "null" then pos = pos + 4 return nil
            end
            local s, e = text:find("^-?[%d%.eE+-]+", pos)
            pos = e + 1
            return tonumber(text:sub(s, e))
        end
        return value()
    end
    -- the value of a track at a time: linear between keyframes, the first / last value outside them, the latest keyframe for sprites.
    -- Time only moves forward while a clip plays, so each track remembers the keyframe it was at and the search starts there (a clip of
    -- hundreds of keyframes per track used to be walked from the start for every target every frame). Returns the value, or two numbers
    -- (x, y) for a pair, without making a table.
    local function sample(track, time)
        local k = track.keyframes
        local n = #k
        if n == 0 then return nil end
        local i = track.cur or 2
        if i < 2 or i > n or time < k[i - 1][1] then i = 2 end
        if time <= k[1][1] then track.cur = 2 local v = k[1][2] if type(v) == "table" then return v[1], v[2] end return v end
        while i <= n and time >= k[i][1] do i = i + 1 end
        track.cur = i <= n and i or n
        if i > n then local v = k[n][2] if type(v) == "table" then return v[1], v[2] end return v end
        local a, b = k[i - 1], k[i]
        if track.type == "DiscreteSprite" then return a[2] end
        local f = (time - a[1]) / (b[1] - a[1])
        if type(a[2]) == "table" then return a[2][1] + (b[2][1] - a[2][1]) * f, a[2][2] + (b[2][2] - a[2][2]) * f end
        return a[2] + (b[2] - a[2]) * f
    end
    env.cutsceneLoad = function(tag, file)
        local text
        local base = file:match("([^/\\]+)$") or file
        for _, path in ipairs({file, file .. ".json", "animations/" .. file, "animations/" .. file .. ".json", "animations/Tutorial/" .. base, "animations/Tutorial/" .. base .. ".json"}) do
            text = env.readDataFile(path)
            if text then break end
        end
        local c = {tag = tag, time = 0, playing = false, x = 0, y = 0, sx = 1, sy = 1, angle = 0, mode = "once", nodes = {}, duration = 0}
        cuts[tag] = c
        if not text then env.print("cutsceneLoad: cannot read " .. file .. "\n") return end
        local ok, doc = pcall(parseJson, text)
        local data = ok and doc and doc.comps and doc.comps[1] and doc.comps[1].data
        c.actions = data and data.actions or {}
    end
    local function buildNodes(c, action)
        local clip = c.actions[action] and c.actions[action].clips and c.actions[action].clips[""]
        c.nodes, c.duration = {}, 0
        if not clip then return end
        local list = {}
        for i, key in ipairs(clip.targets.__order) do
            local layer = key:match("_L(%d+)$")
            local n = {key = key, tracks = clip.targets[key], children = {}}
            n.layer = tonumber(layer)
            list[#list + 1] = n
            for _, track in pairs(n.tracks) do
                if type(track) == "table" and track.keyframes then
                    local last = track.keyframes[#track.keyframes]
                    if last and last[1] > c.duration then c.duration = last[1] end
                end
            end
        end
        -- the parent is the target whose "<name>_<layer>_" the key starts with (the longest one); the rest hang from the first target
        for _, n in ipairs(list) do
            local best
            for _, p in ipairs(list) do
                if p ~= n then
                    local pname = p.key:match("^(.*)_L%d+$")
                    -- the key of a child starts with its parent's name, the parent's layer and an underscore; the name is a tail of the parent's own key
                    for s in pname:gmatch("()[^_]") do
                        local tail = pname:sub(s) .. "_" .. p.layer .. "_"
                        if n.key:sub(1, #tail) == tail and (not best or #tail > best.len) then best = {node = p, len = #tail} end
                    end
                end
            end
            n.parent = best and best.node or (n ~= list[1] and list[1] or nil)
            if n.parent then n.parent.children[#n.parent.children + 1] = n end
        end
        c.nodes = list
        c.root = list[1]
    end
    env.cutsceneStart = function(tag, action, mode)
        local c = cuts[tag]
        if not c or not c.actions then return end
        if not action or not c.actions[action] then action = next(c.actions) end
        buildNodes(c, action)
        c.time, c.playing, c.mode, c.finished = 0, true, mode or "once", false
    end
    env.cutsceneClose = function(tag) cuts[tag] = nil end
    env.cutsceneSetTranslation = function(tag, x, y) local c = cuts[tag] if c then c.x, c.y = x, y end end
    env.cutsceneSetScale = function(tag, sx, sy) local c = cuts[tag] if c then c.sx, c.sy = sx, sy or sx end end
    env.cutsceneSetRotation = function(tag, a) local c = cuts[tag] if c then c.angle = a end end
    env.updateCutscene = function(dt)
        for _, c in pairs(cuts) do
            if c.playing and not c.finished then
                c.time = c.time + dt
                if c.time > c.duration then
                    if c.mode == "repeat" and c.duration > 0 then c.time = c.time % c.duration else c.time, c.finished = c.duration, true end   -- a clip played once stays on its last picture and is not stepped again
                end
            end
        end
    end
    -- cutsceneStop(tag) (0x411500), cutsceneStopAll (0x40d350), cutsceneCloseAll (0x40d340), cutsceneSeek(tag, time) (0x411580)
    env.cutsceneStop = function(tag) local c = cuts[tag] if c then c.playing = false end end
    env.cutsceneStopAll = function() for _, c in pairs(cuts) do c.playing = false end end
    env.cutsceneCloseAll = function() for tag in pairs(cuts) do cuts[tag] = nil end end
    env.cutsceneSeek = function(tag, time) local c = cuts[tag] if c then c.time, c.finished = time or 0, false for _, n in ipairs(c.nodes) do for _, tr in pairs(n.tracks) do if type(tr) == "table" then tr.cur = nil end end end end end
    local function drawNode(c, n, px, py, psx, psy, pang)
        local t = n.tracks
        local pos1, pos2, sc1, sc2, rot = 0, 0, 1, 1, 0
        if t.translation then pos1, pos2 = sample(t.translation, c.time) if not pos1 then pos1, pos2 = 0, 0 end end
        if t.scale then sc1, sc2 = sample(t.scale, c.time) if not sc1 then sc1, sc2 = 1, 1 end end
        if t.rotation then rot = sample(t.rotation, c.time) or 0 end
        local ca, sa = math.cos(pang), math.sin(pang)
        local x = px + (pos1 * psx) * ca - (pos2 * psy) * sa
        local y = py + (pos1 * psx) * sa + (pos2 * psy) * ca
        local sx, sy, ang = psx * sc1, psy * (sc2 or sc1), pang + rot
        local sprite = t.sprite and sample(t.sprite, c.time)
        if sprite and sx ~= 0 and sy ~= 0 then
            env.setRenderState(0, 0, sx, sy, ang, 0, 0, 1)
            env.res.drawSprite(sprite, x / sx, y / sy)
        end
        for i = #n.children, 1, -1 do drawNode(c, n.children[i], x, y, sx, sy, ang) end
    end
    env.drawCutscene = function(tag)
        local c = cuts[tag]
        if not c or not c.root or not c.playing then return end
        drawNode(c, c.root, c.x, c.y, c.sx, c.sy, c.angle)
        env.setRenderState(0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1)
    end
end

-- Star Wars natives of a device or of the metro layout: the PC build answers the way a plain full-screen window does
ifMissing("getFontScale", function() return 1 end)
ifMissing("getUIScale", function() return 1 end)
ifMissing("getWindowState", function() return "FULL" end)
ifMissing("clearParticlesWithTagNative", function() env.clearParticles() end)
for _, n in ipairs({"tryUnsnap", "sendTweet", "setAccelerometerSensitivity", "setNotificationsEnabled", "getLeaderboardScoresAroundPlayer",
                    "getLeaderboardScoresForFriends"}) do ifMissing(n, function() end) end
if env.res then
    if env.res.getClipRect == nil then env.res.getClipRect = function() return 0, 0, env.screenWidth, env.screenHeight end end
    if env.res.createSystemFont == nil then env.res.createSystemFont = function() end end
end
```

`src/lua/stella_natives.lua`:

```lua
-- Angry Birds Stella 1.0.0 (iPhone .ipa): the natives its scripts call that the exe had and this engine has not.
-- Stella is built on the Star Wars II code (gravity filters, Yoda force objects ...) with new services: Skynest (the Rovio account and
-- cloud saves), the social manager, the Telepods scanner, Flash animations (AnimationWrapperNative) and the shader parameters.
-- Online services answer "not available" or "not logged in"; the rest do the nearest thing the engine can.
local env = ...
local _G = _G
local none = function() end
local no = function() return false end

-- a table whose missing functions do nothing (and answer nil): the services the game asks about but cannot use here
local function module(name, fields)
    local t = fields or {}
    return setmetatable(t, {__index = function(_, k) return none end})
end
local function global(name, t)
    if rawget(_G, name) == nil then rawset(_G, name, t) end
    if rawget(env, name) == nil then rawset(env, name, rawget(_G, name)) end
end

-- table.remove as in Lua 5.1.5, which Stella was built with: a position outside 1..#t removes nothing. The engine's Lua (5.1.4) then
-- cleared the last element instead; the camera code removes its temporary camera (kept at index 99) that way, and losing the castle
-- camera stopped every shot when the bird was released
do
    local remove = table.remove
    table.remove = function(t, pos)
        if pos ~= nil then
            local n = #t
            if pos < 1 or pos > n then return end
        end
        return remove(t, pos)
    end
end

-- the render state the scripts set last: the Flash animations and the scaled sprite draws below set their own transform, keep the
-- scripts' transparency (the slingshot's pig highlight is drawn at alpha 0 until the player aims) and put the scripts' state back afterwards
local nativeSetRenderState = env.setRenderState
local renderArgs = {n = 0}
env.setRenderState = function(...)
    renderArgs = {n = select("#", ...), ...}
    return nativeSetRenderState(...)
end
local function scriptAlpha()
    local a = renderArgs.n >= 8 and renderArgs[8] or 1
    return type(a) == "number" and a or 1
end
local function restoreRenderState() nativeSetRenderState(unpack(renderArgs, 1, renderArgs.n)) end

-- shaders: the scripts ask for numbered copies of a shader ("2d-sprite-gold#1" ...) and set parameters on them (Shader.lua keeps those in Lua);
-- the drawing here has no shaders, so the names are only names
if env.createUniqueShaders == nil then
    env.createUniqueShaders = function(name, count)
        local list = {}
        for i = 1, count or 1 do list[i] = tostring(name) .. "#" .. i end
        return list
    end
end

-- ResourceManager: the sprite sheets and sounds go through the engine's own res functions
local res = _G.res
local nativePlay = res.playAudio      -- (the game puts its own playAudio into res.playAudio, which calls native_playAudio)
global("ResourceManager", module("ResourceManager", {
    native_createSpriteSheet = function(...) return res.createSpriteSheet(...) end,
    native_releaseSpriteSheet = function(...) return res.releaseSpriteSheet(...) end,
    native_createAudio = function(...) return res.createAudio and res.createAudio(...) end,
    native_createAudioFromAppData = function(...) return res.createAudio and res.createAudio(...) end,
    native_releaseAudio = function(...) return res.releaseAudio and res.releaseAudio(...) end,
    native_playAudio = function(...) return nativePlay(...) end,
}))
-- playAudioReturnUniqueHandle(name, volume, loop, pan): soundManager.lua keeps the native at load time; the clip name is the handle
-- (fadeAudioClip / setAudioClipVolume take it back)
if env.playAudioReturnUniqueHandle == nil then
    env.playAudioReturnUniqueHandle = function(name, volume, loop)
        if type(name) ~= "string" then return nil end
        nativePlay(name, volume or 1, loop and true or false)
        return name
    end
end
if env.setAudioClipVolume == nil then env.setAudioClipVolume = function(h, v) if type(h) == "string" then res.setAudioClipVolume(h, v or 1) end end end
if env.setMusicVolume == nil then env.setMusicVolume = none end
global("Assets", module("Assets", {
    createSpriteSheet = function(...) return res.createSpriteSheet(...) end,
    loadFiles = function(list, callback) if type(callback) == "function" then callback(true) end return true end,
}))

-- online services: not here
global("SkynestAccount", module("SkynestAccount", {native_isLoggedIn = no}))
global("SkynestStorage", module("SkynestStorage", {native_isTransactionInProcess = no}))
global("CloudSync", module("CloudSync", {}))

    getFriendProgressForLevel = function() return {} end, isAvatarInGraphicsMemory = no}))

-- EconomyParameters.loadConfiguration(file): the prices and rewards (config/economy.dat, plain JSON) are handed to economyParametersLoaded;

global("EconomyParameters", module("EconomyParameters", {

        if type(t) == "table" and type(env.economyParametersLoaded) == "function" then env.economyParametersLoaded(t) end
    end,

global("GiftBirdSkins", module("GiftBirdSkins", {}))
global("ParticleEditorNative", module("ParticleEditorNative", {}))

if env.copyFileFromBundleToAppData == nil then env.copyFileFromBundleToAppData = function() return true end end   -- (the game then reads the bundle's copy)

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- AnimationWrapperNative: the Flash animations (animations/<name>.anim.json and .skins.json, exported from Spine: a tree of entities
-- (bones), slots that show a sprite, and actions whose tracks move them). The exe played and drew them; this is a player in Lua.
--   entity tracks: translation (LinearFloat2), rotation (LinearFloat, radians), scale (LinearFloat2)
--   slot tracks:   sprite (DiscreteString), alpha (LinearFloat), zOrder (DiscreteInt); spineEvent (DiscreteString) on any entity
--   skins:         skins[skin][slot name without SLOT_][sprite] = {x, y}: where the sprite's centre sits on its slot
-- The animation is drawn at the translation / rotation / scale the scripts set (screen pixels), y down.
local floor, sin, cos, abs = math.floor, math.sin, math.cos, math.abs
local files = {}         -- parsed files by name
local anims = {}         -- by tag

local function parse(file)
    if files[file] ~= nil then return files[file] end
    local data = env.abReadJson and env.abReadJson(file)
    if type(data) ~= "table" then files[file] = false return false end
    local f = {entities = {}, order = {}, actions = {}, skins = {}}
    local function walk(node, parent)
        if type(node) ~= "table" then return end
        if node.name then
            local e = {name = node.name, parent = parent, index = #f.order + 1, slot = string.sub(node.name, 1, 5) == "SLOT_"}
            f.entities[node.name] = e
            f.order[#f.order + 1] = e
            parent = e
        end
        if type(node.children) == "table" then for _, c in ipairs(node.children) do walk(c, parent) end end
    end
    walk(data, nil)
    for _, comp in ipairs(type(data.comps) == "table" and data.comps or {}) do
        local acts = type(comp.data) == "table" and comp.data.actions
        if type(acts) == "table" then
            for name, a in pairs(acts) do
                local targets, length = {}, 0
                for _, clip in pairs(type(a.clips) == "table" and a.clips or {}) do
                    for tname, tracks in pairs(type(clip.targets) == "table" and clip.targets or {}) do
                        targets[tname] = targets[tname] or {}
                        for k, tr in pairs(tracks) do
                            targets[tname][k] = tr
                            local kf = tr.keyframes
                            if type(kf) == "table" and #kf > 0 and kf[#kf][1] > length then length = kf[#kf][1] end
                        end
                    end
                end
                f.actions[name] = {targets = targets, length = length}
            end
        end
    end
    local skinFile = string.gsub(file, "%.anim%.json$", ".skins.json")
    local skins = skinFile ~= file and env.abReadJson and env.abReadJson(skinFile)
    if type(skins) == "table" then f.skins = skins end
    files[file] = f
    return f
end

-- a track's value at time t: discrete tracks keep the last key at or before t, linear ones blend the two around it
local function sample(track, t)
    local kf = track.keyframes
    if type(kf) ~= "table" or #kf == 0 then return nil end
    if t <= kf[1][1] then return kf[1][2] end
    local n = #kf
    if t >= kf[n][1] then return kf[n][2] end
    local lo, hi = 1, n
    while hi - lo > 1 do local mid = floor((lo + hi) / 2) if kf[mid][1] <= t then lo = mid else hi = mid end end
    local a, b = kf[lo], kf[hi]
    if string.sub(track.type or "", 1, 8) == "Discrete" then return a[2] end
    local span = b[1] - a[1]
    local k = span > 0 and (t - a[1]) / span or 0
    if type(a[2]) == "table" then return {a[2][1] + (b[2][1] - a[2][1]) * k, a[2][2] + (b[2][2] - a[2][2]) * k} end
    return a[2] + (b[2] - a[2]) * k
end

-- the pose of every entity at the animation's time: local values from the action's tracks (kept from the last action that set them)
local function pose(a)
    local f = a.data
    if not f then return end
    local act = a.action and f.actions[a.action]
    a.state = a.state or {}
    for _, e in ipairs(f.order) do
        local s = a.state[e.name]
        if not s then s = {x = 0, y = 0, r = 0, sx = 1, sy = 1, alpha = 1, z = e.index} a.state[e.name] = s end
        local tr = act and act.targets[e.name]
        if tr then
            local v
            if tr.translation then v = sample(tr.translation, a.time) if v then s.x, s.y = v[1], v[2] end end
            if tr.rotation then v = sample(tr.rotation, a.time) if v then s.r = v end end
            if tr.scale then v = sample(tr.scale, a.time) if v then s.sx, s.sy = v[1], v[2] end end
            if tr.alpha then v = sample(tr.alpha, a.time) if v then s.alpha = v end end
            if tr.sprite then v = sample(tr.sprite, a.time) if v ~= nil then s.sprite = v end end
            if tr.zOrder then v = sample(tr.zOrder, a.time) if v then s.z = v end end
        end
    end
    -- world (animation space) transforms, parents first (the tree order puts them first)
    for _, e in ipairs(f.order) do
        local s = a.state[e.name]
        local p = e.parent and a.state[e.parent.name]
        if p then
            local c, n = cos(p.wr), sin(p.wr)
            local lx, ly = s.x * p.wsx, s.y * p.wsy
            s.wx, s.wy = p.wx + c * lx - n * ly, p.wy + n * lx + c * ly
            s.wr, s.wsx, s.wsy, s.walpha = p.wr + s.r, p.wsx * s.sx, p.wsy * s.sy, p.walpha * s.alpha
        else
            s.wx, s.wy, s.wr, s.wsx, s.wsy, s.walpha = s.x, s.y, s.r, s.sx, s.sy, s.alpha
        end
    end
end

local function fire(a, event, ...)
    if type(a.handler) == "function" then
        local ok, err = pcall(a.handler, a.tag, a.action, event, ...)
        if not ok then print("animation event " .. tostring(event) .. ": " .. tostring(err)) end
    end
end

-- the spine events whose key time was passed between t0 and t1 ("playAudio:::sound" is the event playAudio with the parts after it)
local function events(a, t0, t1)
    local act = a.data and a.action and a.data.actions[a.action]
    if not act then return end
    for _, tr in pairs(act.targets) do
        local ev = tr.spineEvent
        if ev and type(ev.keyframes) == "table" then
            for _, k in ipairs(ev.keyframes) do
                if k[1] > t0 and k[1] <= t1 and type(k[2]) == "string" and k[2] ~= "" then
                    local parts = {}
                    for piece in string.gmatch(k[2] .. ":", "([^:]*):") do parts[#parts + 1] = piece end
                    fire(a, parts[1], select(2, unpack(parts)))
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

local function get(tag) return anims[tag] end
local function load(tag, file)
    local a = anims[tag] or {tag = tag, tx = 0, ty = 0, rot = 0, sx = 1, sy = 1, speed = 1, time = 0, skin = "default"}
    a.file, a.data, a.action, a.playing, a.time, a.state, a.placed = file, parse(file) or nil, nil, false, 0, nil, nil
    anims[tag] = a
    return a
end

local W = {}
W.preloadFromBundle = function(file) parse(file) end
W.preloadFromAppData = W.preloadFromBundle
W.loadFromBundle = function(tag, file) load(tag, file) end
W.loadFromAppData = W.loadFromBundle
W.close = function(tag) anims[tag] = nil end
W.clearCache = function() files = {} end
W.setPlaybackEvent = function(tag, handler) local a = get(tag) if a then a.handler = handler end end
W.start = function(tag, action, mode)
    local a = get(tag)
    if not a then return end
    a.action, a.mode, a.time, a.playing, a.paused = action, mode or "once", 0, true, false
    pose(a)
    events(a, -1, 0)
end
W.stop = function(tag) local a = get(tag) if a then a.playing = false end end
W.pause = function(tag) local a = get(tag) if a then a.paused = true end end
W.resume = function(tag) local a = get(tag) if a then a.paused = false end end
W.isPlaying = function(tag) local a = get(tag) return a ~= nil and a.playing == true end
W.seek = function(tag, t) local a = get(tag) if a then a.time = t or 0 pose(a) end end
W.setSpeed = function(tag, s) local a = get(tag) if a then a.speed = s or 1 end end
W.setTranslation = function(tag, x, y) local a = get(tag) if a then a.tx, a.ty, a.placed = x or 0, y or 0, true end end
W.setRotation = function(tag, r) local a = get(tag) if a then a.rot = r or 0 end end
W.setScale = function(tag, sx, sy) local a = get(tag) if a then a.sx, a.sy = sx or 1, sy or sx or 1 end end
W.setShader = function(tag, s) local a = get(tag) if a then a.shader = s end end
W.setSkin = function(tag, s) local a = get(tag) if a then a.skin = s or "default" end end
W.getActions = function(tag)
    local a = get(tag)
    local list = {}
    if a and a.data then for name in pairs(a.data.actions) do list[#list + 1] = name end end
    table.sort(list)
    return list
end
W.containsEntity = function(tag, name) local a = get(tag) return a ~= nil and a.data and a.data.entities[name] ~= nil or false end

local function entityState(tag, name)
    local a = get(tag)
    if not (a and a.data and a.data.entities[name]) then return nil end
    if not a.state then pose(a) end
    return a.state and a.state[name]
end
-- the entity in the animation's own space: x, y, scaleX, scaleY, angle
W.getEntityWorldTransform = function(tag, name)
    local s = entityState(tag, name)
    if not s then return nil end
    return s.wx, s.wy, s.wsx, s.wsy, s.wr
end
W.getEntityWorldPosition = function(tag, name) local s = entityState(tag, name) if s then return s.wx, s.wy end return 0, 0 end
W.getEntityPosition = function(tag, name) local s = entityState(tag, name) if s then return s.x, s.y end return 0, 0 end
W.getEntityScale = function(tag, name) local s = entityState(tag, name) if s then return s.wsx, s.wsy end return 1, 1 end

W.update = function(dt)
    dt = dt or 0
    for _, a in pairs(anims) do
        if a.playing and not a.paused and a.data then
            local act = a.action and a.data.actions[a.action]
            local length = act and act.length or 0
            local t0 = a.time
            a.time = a.time + dt * (a.speed or 1)
            if a.time >= length then
                events(a, t0, length)
                if a.mode == "repeat" and length > 0 then
                    a.time = a.time % length
                    events(a, -1, a.time)
                else
                    a.time = length
                    a.playing = false
                    pose(a)
                    fire(a, "PLAYBACK_END")
                end
            else
                events(a, t0, a.time)
            end
            pose(a)
        end
    end
end

local function offsetOf(f, skin, slot, sprite)
    local key = string.sub(slot, 6)
    for _, name in ipairs({skin, "default"}) do
        local sk = f.skins[name]
        local slotSkin = type(sk) == "table" and sk[key]
        local o = type(slotSkin) == "table" and slotSkin[sprite]
        if type(o) == "table" then return o.x or 0, o.y or 0 end
    end
    return 0, 0
end

-- a slot's sprite rectangle in the animation's space: left, top, right, bottom. The sprite's centre sits at its skin offset from the
-- slot (the comic cutscenes clip each panel to its border slot, whose entity point is shared by all four borders)
W.getEntityWorldBounds = function(tag, name)
    local s = entityState(tag, name)
    if not (s and s.sprite and s.sprite ~= "") then return 0, 0, 0, 0 end
    local a = get(tag)
    local w, h = 0, 0
    if res.getSpriteBounds then w, h = res.getSpriteBounds(s.sprite) w, h = w or 0, h or 0 end
    local ox, oy = offsetOf(a.data, a.skin, name, s.sprite)
    local cr, sr = cos(s.wr), sin(s.wr)
    local ax, ay = ox * s.wsx, oy * s.wsy
    local cx, cy = s.wx + cr * ax - sr * ay, s.wy + sr * ax + cr * ay
    local hw, hh = w * abs(s.wsx) / 2, h * abs(s.wsy) / 2
    local ex, ey = abs(cr) * hw + abs(sr) * hh, abs(sr) * hw + abs(cr) * hh
    return cx - ex, cy - ey, cx + ex, cy + ey
end

W.draw = function(tag, objectAlpha)
    local a = get(tag)
    if not (a and a.data) then return end
    if not a.state then pose(a) end
    local f = a.data
    local alpha = objectAlpha or scriptAlpha()        -- (a cutscene or the scripts fading the animation out; an object draws at its own)
    local slots = {}
    for _, e in ipairs(f.order) do
        local s = a.state[e.name]
        if e.slot and s.sprite and s.sprite ~= "" and s.walpha > 0 then slots[#slots + 1] = e end
    end
    -- a larger zOrder is further back (the comic panels: 10 the picture, 1-4 its borders; Stella: 18 the body, 14-17 the eyes and beak)
    table.sort(slots, function(p, q) local zp, zq = a.state[p.name].z, a.state[q.name].z if zp ~= zq then return zp > zq end return p.index < q.index end)
    local c, n = cos(a.rot), sin(a.rot)
    for _, e in ipairs(slots) do
        local s = a.state[e.name]
        local ox, oy = offsetOf(f, a.skin, e.name, s.sprite)
        -- the sprite's centre in animation space, then on the screen
        local cr, sr = cos(s.wr), sin(s.wr)
        local ax, ay = ox * s.wsx, oy * s.wsy
        local px, py = s.wx + cr * ax - sr * ay, s.wy + sr * ax + cr * ay
        px, py = px * a.sx, py * a.sy
        local X, Y = a.tx + c * px - n * py, a.ty + n * px + c * py
        local ksx, ksy = s.wsx * a.sx, s.wsy * a.sy
        local w, h = 0, 0
        if res.getSpriteBounds then w, h = res.getSpriteBounds(s.sprite) end
        if w and w > 0 and ksx ~= 0 and ksy ~= 0 then
            nativeSetRenderState(0, 0, ksx, ksy, s.wr + a.rot, w / 2, h / 2, s.walpha * alpha)
            res.drawSprite(s.sprite, X / ksx - w / 2, Y / ksy - h / 2, "TOP", "LEFT")   -- (the default puts the pivot there)
        end
    end
    restoreRenderState()
end
W.debugAnimations = function() return anims end      -- (console: the playing animations by tag)
global("AnimationWrapperNative", module("AnimationWrapperNative", W))

-- Align.getPositionAndScale(spec, refW, refH, screenW, screenH): a layout point given on the reference screen (posx, posy, scalex, scaley,
-- alignH LEFT / CENTER / RIGHT, alignV TOP / CENTER / BOTTOM) on the real screen: the reference is scaled to fit and every point keeps its
-- distance from the edge (or the middle) it is aligned to. Returns x, y, scaleX, scaleY
global("Align", module("Align", {
    getPositionAndScale = function(spec, rw, rh, sw, sh)
        spec = spec or {}
        rw, rh, sw, sh = rw or 1024, rh or 768, sw or rw or 1024, sh or rh or 768
        local k = math.min(sw / rw, sh / rh)
        local px, py = spec.posx or 0, spec.posy or 0
        local x, y
        if spec.alignH == "LEFT" then x = px * k elseif spec.alignH == "RIGHT" then x = sw - (rw - px) * k else x = sw / 2 + (px - rw / 2) * k end
        if spec.alignV == "TOP" then y = py * k elseif spec.alignV == "BOTTOM" then y = sh - (rh - py) * k else y = sh / 2 + (py - rh / 2) * k end
        return x, y, (spec.scalex or 1) * k, (spec.scaley or 1) * k
    end,
}))

-- createNonPhysicsObject(name, sprite, x, y, zOrder): an object that is only drawn (menu pieces, decorations): here a small static box that
-- collides with nothing
local drawnOnly = {}      -- name -> sprite of the objects made by createNonPhysicsObject
if env.createNonPhysicsObject == nil then
    env.createNonPhysicsObject = function(name, sprite, x, y, z)
        env.createBox(name, sprite, x, y, 0.1, 0.1, 0, 0, 0, false, false, z or 0)     -- (density 0: static, so decorations stay where the level puts them)
        drawnOnly[name] = sprite
    end
end
-- getIntersectingObjects also finds those objects where their sprite is drawn (the menu's play button, the map's level buttons are
-- tapped through it: BlockPointerEventSubsystem); the exe tested their sprite rectangles
local intersecting = env.getIntersectingObjects
if intersecting then
    env.getIntersectingObjects = function(q)
        local list = intersecting(q) or {}
        if type(q) ~= "table" then return list end
        local world = type(env.objects) == "table" and env.objects.world
        if type(world) ~= "table" then return list end
        local seen = {}
        for _, n in ipairs(list) do seen[n] = true end
        local ps = env.physicsScale or 0.05
        local qx, qy = q.x or 0, q.y or 0
        local l, r, d, u = math.abs(q.left or 0), math.abs(q.right or 0), math.abs(q.down or 0), math.abs(q.up or 0)
        local candidates = {}
        for name, sprite in pairs(drawnOnly) do if world[name] == nil then drawnOnly[name] = nil else candidates[name] = sprite end end
        if env.getObjectDefinition then      -- and the tappable objects (onPress / onTap / onDrag), which collide with nothing
            for name, o in pairs(world) do
                if type(o) == "table" and candidates[name] == nil then
                    local def = env.getObjectDefinition(name)
                    if type(def) == "table" and (def.onPress or def.onTap or def.onDrag) then candidates[name] = o.sprite end
                end
            end
        end
        for name, sprite in pairs(candidates) do
            local o = world[name]
            if not seen[name] and sprite and (not env.isVisible or env.isVisible(name)) then
                local w, h = 0, 0
                if res.getSpriteBounds then w, h = res.getSpriteBounds(o.sprite or sprite) w, h = w or 0, h or 0 end
                local px, py = w / 2, h / 2
                if res.getSpritePivot then local a, b = res.getSpritePivot(o.sprite or sprite) px, py = a or px, b or py end
                local sx, sy = 1, 1
                if env.getScale then local a, b = env.getScale(name) sx, sy = a or 1, b or a or 1 end
                local x, y = o.x or 0, o.y or 0
                local x1, x2 = x - px * sx * ps, x + (w - px) * sx * ps
                local y1, y2 = y - py * sy * ps, y + (h - py) * sy * ps
                if qx + r >= x1 and qx - l <= x2 and qy + u >= y1 and qy - d <= y2 then list[#list + 1] = name end
            end
        end
        return list
    end
end

-- setFlashAnimation(object [, file, action]): the object is drawn as the Flash animation with its name as the tag instead of its sprite.
-- With a file (a block whose definition has flashAnimation) the animation is loaded here and follows the object; without one a
-- FlashAnimationWrapper of the scripts plays it and places it (attach). removeFlashAnimation(object) draws the sprite again.
local flashObjects = {}
def("setFlashAnimation", function(name, file, action)
    if type(name) ~= "string" then return end
    flashObjects[name] = true
    if type(file) == "string" then
        local a = load(name, file)
        if a.data then
            if not (action and a.data.actions[action]) then action = W.getActions(name)[1] end

env.engine.drawObject = function(name, ...)
    if flashObjects[name] then
        local a = anims[name]
        if a and not a.placed and env.physicsToScreenTransform then     -- (an animation the scripts do not place follows its object)
            local o = env.objects and env.objects.world and env.objects.world[name]
            if o then
                a.tx, a.ty = env.physicsToScreenTransform(o.x, o.y)
                local sx, sy = 1, 1
                if env.getScale then sx, sy = env.getScale(name) sx, sy = sx or 1, sy or sx or 1 end
                local k = env.worldScale or 1
                a.sx, a.sy, a.rot = sx * k, sy * k, (env.getAngle and env.getAngle(name)) or 0
            end
        end
        if a then W.draw(name, 1) end
        return false
    end
    if previousDrawObject then return previousDrawObject(name, ...) end
end
-- drawSpriteWithShader(sprite, shader, x, y, scaleX, scaleY, angle) / drawSpriteWithoutShader(sprite, x, y, scaleX, scaleY, angle): the sprite's
-- pivot at (x, y); the shader (the greyed-out look of a disabled button) is left out
local function drawScaled(sprite, x, y, sx, sy, angle)
    if not sprite then return end
    sx, sy = sx or 1, sy or sx or 1
    if sx == 0 or sy == 0 then return end
    local px, py = 0, 0
    if res.getSpritePivot then px, py = res.getSpritePivot(sprite) px, py = px or 0, py or 0 end
    nativeSetRenderState(0, 0, sx, sy, angle or 0, px, py, scriptAlpha())
    res.drawSprite(sprite, (x or 0) / sx - px, (y or 0) / sy - py, "TOP", "LEFT")
    restoreRenderState()
end
def("drawSpriteWithShader", function(sprite, shader, x, y, sx, sy, angle) drawScaled(sprite, x, y, sx, sy, angle) end)
def("drawSpriteWithoutShader", function(sprite, x, y, sx, sy, angle) drawScaled(sprite, x, y, sx, sy, angle) end)
def("deviceManufacturer", "Apple")
def("deviceInfoModel", "iPhone")

-- v3.2: leaving a level (Next after level 3, a level picked on the map) could call GameScene:onExit a second time. The first call
-- removes the scene's listeners and drops the slingshot; the second found neither (an EventManager "nonexistant listener" error for
-- each event) and then stopped on the missing slingshot, so the scene change was tried again every frame and the game hung. A scene
-- that has already left does nothing on a second onExit; onEntry makes it leavable again.
local function guardScene(scene)
    if type(scene) ~= "table" or rawget(scene, "__abGuarded") then return end
    local onExit, onEntry = rawget(scene, "onExit"), rawget(scene, "onEntry")
    if type(onExit) ~= "function" or type(onEntry) ~= "function" then return end
    scene.__abGuarded = true
    scene.onEntry = function(self, ...) rawset(self, "__abLeft", nil) return onEntry(self, ...) end
    scene.onExit = function(self, ...)
        if rawget(self, "__abLeft") then return end
        rawset(self, "__abLeft", true)
        return onExit(self, ...)
    end
end
guardScene(rawget(env, "GameScene"))
env.abGuardStellaScene = function() guardScene(rawget(env, "GameScene")) end
```

`src/physics/collision_prediction.h`:

```h
#pragma once

namespace ab {

// predictCollision: what would happen if two objects met, worked out from where they are and how they move, before anything touches
struct CollisionPrediction {
    bool valid = false;               // false: one of the objects does not exist (every other field is 0)
    bool collides = false;            // the contact filter lets them collide, and they are moving towards each other
    bool filtered = false;            // the contact filter keeps them apart (a sensor, a collision-less object, Space's masks)
    float distance = 0, gap = 0;      // between the centres / between the surfaces (approximate: circles by radius, other shapes by their boxes)
    float nx = 0, ny = 0;             // contact normal, from A to B
    float relVx = 0, relVy = 0;       // velocity of B seen from A
    float closingSpeed = 0;           // speed along the normal, positive when they approach
    float timeToContact = -1;         // seconds at the current speeds (-1: never)
    float impulse = 0;                // size of the normal impulse of the collision
    float restitution = 0;
    float massA = 0, massB = 0;
    float aVx = 0, aVy = 0, bVx = 0, bVy = 0;   // the velocities after the collision
    float energyLost = 0;             // kinetic energy (linear and spin) that the impact removes
    bool exactShapes = false;         // the contact point and normal come from the closest points of the real shapes (false: the line between the centres)
    float contactX = 0, contactY = 0; // the point where they would touch (halfway between the two surfaces)
    float normalSpeed = 0, tangentSpeed = 0;   // speed of B relative to A at that point, along the normal / along the tangent (nx, ny turned by 90 degrees: ny, -nx), before the hit
    float friction = 0;               // the combined friction coefficient, sqrt(frictionA * frictionB)
    float tangentImpulse = 0;         // the friction impulse along the tangent (clamped to friction * impulse)
    float aAngVel = 0, bAngVel = 0;   // angular velocities after the collision (radians per second)
};

}  // namespace ab

```

`src/physics/physics_world.cpp`:

```cpp
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
// The part of the physics world that does not depend on the Box2D version. See physics_world.h.
#include "physics/physics_world.h"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>

namespace ab {

namespace {
const float kTwoPi = 6.2831855f;
}

std::unique_ptr<PhysicsWorld> MakePhysicsWorld(Box2DVersion version) {
    return version == Box2DVersion::V22 ? MakePhysicsWorld22() : MakePhysicsWorld21();
}

PhysObject* PhysicsWorld::Find(const std::string& name) const {
    auto it = byName_.find(name);
    return it == byName_.end() ? nullptr : it->second;
}

PhysObject* PhysicsWorld::NewObject(const BodyDef& d, float rollFactor, bool circle) {
    // An object that already has this name is replaced in the hash table by the original; the old
    // body stays in the world. Scripts never reuse a name, so that case is not reproduced here.
    PhysObject* o = new PhysObject();
    o->name = d.name;
    o->id = nextId_++;
    idNames_[o->id] = d.name;
    o->isBird = d.controllable;
    o->recordVelocity = !spaceRules;   // Space: only after setRecordVelocity
    o->zOrder = d.zOrder;
    o->sprite = d.sprite;          // createBox/Circle/Polygon: the sprite is looked up when the body is created
    o->rollFactor = rollFactor;
    o->collision = (circle && !spaceRules) ? true : d.collision;
    o->state[0][0] = o->state[1][0] = o->interpX = d.x;
    o->state[0][1] = o->state[1][1] = o->interpY = d.y;
    return o;
}

void PhysicsWorld::AddObject(PhysObject* o, bool bird) {
    o->body = o->pbody.get();
    objects_.emplace_back(o);
    byName_[o->name] = o;
    frame_.objects.push_back(o);
    if (bird) frame_.birds.push_back(o);
    if (bird && spaceRules && o->pbody) o->pbody->SetActive(false);   // 0x4899d2: a controllable object is created inactive (b2Body::SetActive 0x496ad0); the launch script activates it
}

// ---- joints

PhysicsWorld::JointRecord* PhysicsWorld::FindJoint(const std::string& name) {
    for (auto& j : joints_)
        if (j->name == name) return j.get();
    return nullptr;
}

void PhysicsWorld::RebuildJointViews() {
    frame_.joints.clear();
    for (auto& j : joints_) frame_.joints.push_back(j->view.get());
}

void PhysicsWorld::DropJointRecord(void* joint) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < joints_.size(); i++) {
        if (joints_[i]->joint == joint) { joints_.erase(joints_.begin() + i); break; }
    }
    RebuildJointViews();
}

void PhysicsWorld::DestroyJoint(const std::string& name) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < links_.size(); i++) {
        if (links_[i].name == name) { links_.erase(links_.begin() + i); return; }
    }
    JointRecord* r = FindJoint(name);
    if (!r) return;
    void* j = r->joint;
    DropJointRecord(j);            // Box2D only calls the listener for implicit destruction
    DestroyBox2DJoint(j);
}

void PhysicsWorld::Clear() {
    frame_.objects.clear();
    frame_.birds.clear();
    frame_.joints.clear();
    for (auto& o : objects_) DestroyBody(o.get());   // joints go with their bodies (SayGoodbye)
    objects_.clear();
    byName_.clear();
    idNames_.clear();
    joints_.clear();
    links_.clear();
    frame_.accumulator = 0;
}

std::vector<std::string> PhysicsWorld::RemoveObject(const std::string& name) {
    std::vector<std::string> fired;
    PhysObject* o = Find(name);
    if (o) {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < frame_.birds.size(); i++)
            if (frame_.birds[i] == o) { frame_.birds.erase(frame_.birds.begin() + i); break; }
        for (size_t i = 0; i < frame_.objects.size(); i++)
            if (frame_.objects[i] == o) { frame_.objects.erase(frame_.objects.begin() + i); break; }
        for (size_t i = 0; i < sensorPairs_.size();) if (sensorPairs_[i].first == o || sensorPairs_[i].second == o) sensorPairs_.erase(sensorPairs_.begin() + i); else i++;
        DestroyBody(o);        // also destroys the joints on the body
        byName_.erase(name);
        idNames_.erase(o->id);
        for (size_t i = 0; i < objects_.size(); i++)
            if (objects_[i].get() == o) { objects_.erase(objects_.begin() + i); break; }
    }
    for (size_t i = 0; i < links_.size();) {
        if (links_[i].end1 == name) {
            PhysObject* victim = Find(links_[i].end2);
            if (victim) {
                victim->destroyPending = true;
                victim->destroyTimer = links_[i].destroyTimer;
                fired.push_back(links_[i].name);
                links_.erase(links_.begin() + i);
                continue;
            }
        }
        i++;
    }
    return fired;
}

// ---- per-object calls

void PhysicsWorld::ApplyImpulse(const std::string& n, float ix, float iy, float px, float py) {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (o) o->pbody->ApplyImpulse(ix, iy, px, py);
}

void PhysicsWorld::ApplyForce(const std::string& n, float fx, float fy, float px, float py) {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (o) o->pbody->ApplyForce(fx, fy, px, py);
}

bool PhysicsWorld::SetPosition(const std::string& n, float x, float y) {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (!o) return false;
    o->pbody->SetTransform(x, y, o->pbody->Angle());
    o->state[0][0] = o->state[1][0] = o->interpX = x;
    o->state[0][1] = o->state[1][1] = o->interpY = y;
    return true;
}

bool PhysicsWorld::SetRotation(const std::string& n, float angle, float& normalized) {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (!o) return false;
    float a = std::fmod(angle, kTwoPi);
    if (a < 0) a += kTwoPi;
    o->pbody->SetTransform(o->pbody->PosX(), o->pbody->PosY(), a);
    o->state[0][2] = o->state[1][2] = o->interpAngle = a;
    normalized = a;
    return true;
}

void PhysicsWorld::SetVelocity(const std::string& n, float vx, float vy) {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (o && !o->pbody->IsStatic()) o->pbody->SetLinearVelocity(vx, vy);
}

void PhysicsWorld::SetAngularVelocity(const std::string& n, float w) {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (o && !o->pbody->IsStatic()) o->pbody->SetAngularVelocity(w);
}

bool PhysicsWorld::BodyCommand(const std::string& n, int cmd, float a, float& result) {
    if (cmd == 8) { gravityForceMultiplier = a; return true; }
    if (cmd == 9) { result = gravityForceMultiplier; return true; }
    if (cmd == 90) { waterForceMultiplier = a; return true; }          // setWaterForceMultiplier 0x40d490
    if (cmd == 91) { result = waterForceMultiplier; return true; }     // getWaterForceMultiplier 0x40d4a0
    if (cmd == 92) { birdWaterDrag = a; return true; }                 // 0x40d4b0
    if (cmd == 93) { objectWaterDrag = a; return true; }               // 0x40d4c0
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (!o) return false;
    PhysBody& b = *o->pbody;
    if (cmd == 95) { result = (float)b.Type(); return true; }          // 3.7.1: getBodyType
    if (cmd == 30) { o->filterMask = (int)a; o->filterUsed = true; return true; }   // setFilterMask (3.x)
    if (cmd == 31) { o->filterCat = (int)a; o->filterUsed = true; return true; }    // setFilterCategory (3.x)
    if (cmd == 10) { o->gravMask = (int)a; return true; }
    if (cmd == 11) { o->gravCat = (int)a; return true; }
    if (cmd == 12) { o->gravMin = a; return true; }
    if (cmd == 13) { o->gravMax = a; return true; }
    if (cmd == 14) { o->revertGravity = a != 0; return true; }        // setRevertGravity 0x47a660 (+0x18a)
    if (cmd == 15) { o->revertMulti = a != 0; return true; }          // setRevertGravityWithMultiplier 0x47a6d0 (+0x18b; the multiplier is stored negated at +0x18c, the speed limit at +0x190)
    if (cmd == 16) { o->revertMult = -a; return true; }
    if (cmd == 17) { o->revertMaxSpeed = a; return true; }
    switch (cmd) {
    case 1: b.SetLinearDamping(a); break;
    case 2: b.SetAngularDamping(a); break;
    case 3: b.SetFixedRotation(a != 0); break;
    case 4: b.SetActive(a != 0); break;
    case 5: if (!b.IsStatic()) b.SetLinearVelocity(b.VelX() * a, b.VelY() * a); break;
    case 6: result = b.AngularVelocity(); break;
    case 7: b.SetSensor(a != 0); o->isSensor = a != 0; break;
    default: return false;
    }
    return true;
}

void PhysicsWorld::SetSleeping(const std::string& n, bool sleeping) {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (o) o->pbody->SetAwake(!sleeping);   // false: also zeroes velocities, force and torque
}

float PhysicsWorld::GetAngle(const std::string& n) const {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    return o ? o->interpAngle : 0.0f;
}

void PhysicsWorld::GetWorldPoint(const std::string& n, float lx, float ly, float& wx, float& wy) const {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (!o) { wx = lx; wy = ly; return; }
    o->pbody->WorldPoint(lx, ly, wx, wy);
}

void PhysicsWorld::SetRolling(const std::string& n, int material, bool rolls, float rollFactor) {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (!o) return;
    o->rollMaterial = material;
    o->rolls = rolls;
    o->rollFactor = rollFactor;
}

void PhysicsWorld::SetObjectParameter(const std::string& n, int id, float value) {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (!o) return;
    if (id == 9000) {   // the body type (setBodyType): 0 static, 1 dynamic, 2 kinematic
        if (!o->pbody) return;
        if ((int)value == 2) o->pbody->SetKinematic(); else o->pbody->SetStatic((int)value == 0);
        return;
    }
    if (spaceRules) {
        // 0x47ac60 (jump table at 0x47afe0). Scale is always drawn in Space (ids 5, 17, 18); 6/7 are floats the draw code does not read here,
        // 16 is ignoreClassicGravity (the world has no gravity) and 33 is isVisible
        switch (id) {
        case 1: o->drawWithBirds = (int)value == 1; break;
        case 2: o->pbody->SetStatic(value == 0.0f); break;
        case 5: o->scaleX = o->scaleY = value; o->wobDX = o->wobDY = 0; break;
        case 17: o->scaleX = value; break;
        case 18: o->scaleY = value; break;
        case 8: o->flipX = o->flipBase = (int)value == 1; break;
        case 9: o->enableFlipping = (int)value == 1; break;
        case 10: o->disableRotation = (int)value == 1; break;
        case 11: if (starWarsRules) o->noHitWobble = (int)value == 1; break;   // Star Wars +0x150
        case 12: if (starWarsRules) o->ignoreMoving = (int)value == 1; break;   // Star Wars +0x151
        case 15: o->disableImmovable = (int)value == 1; break;
        case 6: if (starWarsRules) o->bounceAmp = value; break;    // Star Wars +0x108: the multiplier of the hit wobble (blocks' bounceAmplitudeMultiplier)
        case 7: if (starWarsRules) o->bounceFreq = value; break;   // +0x104
        case 36: o->groupIndex = (int)value; break;      // Star Wars: collisionGroupIndex (+0xf4)
        case 16:                                         // Star Wars: ignoreClassicGravity, the body's gravity scale (+0x8c) is 0 for 1, else 1
            if ((int)value == 1) { o->ownGravityMode = 2; o->ownGravityScale = 0; } else if (o->ownGravityMode == 2) o->ownGravityScale = 1;
            break;
        // the Star Wars natives that set one flag of the object record; the script layer maps them to these ids (200 and up are the engine's own)
        case 200: o->blockCollision = (int)value == 1; break;     // native_setBlockCollisionEnabled (+0x154)
        case 201: o->ignoresScore = (int)value == 1; break;       // native_setIgnoresScore (+0x166)
        case 202: o->keepOrientation = (int)value == 1; break;    // native_setKeepOrientation (+0x164)
        case 203: o->affectedByForceMult = (int)value == 1; break; // native_setAffectedByForceMultipliers (+0x165)
        case 204: o->isWater = (int)value == 1; break;            // native_setIsWater (+0x163)
        case 205: o->waterDensity = value; break;                 // native_setWaterDensity (+0x168)
        case 206: o->isBird = (int)value == 1; break;             // native_setControlled (+0x155)
        case 207: o->birdGravReduce = value; break;               // native_setTimeSinceCollision (+0x138)
        case 19: o->spaceFlagA = (int)value == 1; break;
        case 20: o->spaceActive19e = (int)value == 1; break;
        case 21: o->sensorKind = (int)value; break;
        case 22: o->gravOn = (int)value == 1; break;
        case 25: o->gravMin = value; break;
        case 26: o->gravMax = value; break;
        case 27: o->gravRadius = value; break;
        case 35: o->gravExt = value; break; // +0x178 height = field extent
        case 24: case 28: case 29: break; // isBox +0x164, width +0x174, forceAngle +0x17c: stored only, not read by gravity
        case 31: o->birdGravReduce = value; break;
        case 34: o->stopOnExit = (int)value == 1; break;   // +0x1a5
        case 33: o->hidden = (int)value != 1; break;
        default: break;
        }
        return;
    }
    if (id == 1) {
        o->drawWithBirds = (int)value == 1;
    } else if (id == 2) {
        o->pbody->SetStatic(value == 0.0f);
    } else if (id == 5) {
        o->scaleX = o->scaleY = value;
        o->wobDX = o->wobDY = 0;        // the exe sets the current scale together with the base scale
    } else if (id == 6) {
        o->scaled = (int)value == 1;
    } else if (id == 106) {
        o->bounceAmp = value;
    } else if (id == 107) {
        o->bounceFreq = value;
    } else if (id == 8) {
        o->flipX = o->flipBase = (int)value == 1;
    } else if (id == 9) {
        o->enableFlipping = (int)value == 1;
    } else if (id == 10) {
        o->disableRotation = (int)value == 1;      // 0x41b2c0 draws the sprite upright; the physics is untouched
    } else if (id == 14) {
        o->canGetUp = (int)value == 1;
    } else if (id == 15) {
        o->disableImmovable = (int)value == 1;
    } else if (id == 16) {
        o->disableControllable = (int)value == 1;
    } else if (id == 21) {
        o->sensorKind = (int)value;
    } else if (id == 22) {
        o->gravOn = (int)value == 1;
    } else if (id == 25) {
        o->gravMin = value;
    } else if (id == 26) {
        o->gravMax = value;
    } else if (id == 27) {
        o->gravRadius = value;
    }
}

// 0x46f720: a gravitation sensor (kind 2) pulls every dynamic object it touches towards its centre with a force that falls off
// linearly from gravMax at the centre to gravMin at the radius (F = max - |d| / radius * (max - min)), scaled by the object's mass
// and 0.1 and by the game's gravity force multiplier. A sensor without a radius is a field: the force points along its angle.
float PhysicsWorld::BirdGravityFactor(float timer) const {
    if (timer < 0) return gravityForceMultiplier;                     // 0x46f900: before any collision the timer is -1 and the full multiplier applies
    float m = gravityForceMultiplier - timer * Tn("gravity.birdDecay", 1.3f);
    return m > 1 ? m : 1;
}

// The force one gravitation sensor puts on one object (the body of 0x46f720, shared by the real physics and by the aim trail so that the two can never
// disagree). `s` is the sensor, `t` the pulled object, (tx, ty) / (tvx, tvy) its position and velocity, `timer` its bird gravity timer (-1: no
// collision yet) and `mass` its mass. Returns false when the sensor does not pull it (it does not take part in the gravity category, the speed limit
// of setRevertGravityWithMultiplier is reached, the centre of a radial field is hit exactly); otherwise (fx, fy) is the force to apply at the
// object's position. Radial sensors (a radius was set) pull towards their centre with max - distance / radius * (max - min); sensors without a radius are
// directional fields pulling along the axis (-sin, cos) of their angle, measured from the point half an extent along that axis.
bool PhysicsWorld::GravityPull(const PhysObject& s, const PhysObject& t, float tx, float ty, float tvx, float tvy, float timer, float mass, float& fx, float& fy) const {
    if (s.gravMask > -1 && t.gravCat > -1 && (s.gravMask & t.gravCat) == 0) return false;
    float F, ux, uy;
    if (s.gravRadius > -1) {
        float dx = s.pbody->PosX() - tx, dy = s.pbody->PosY() - ty;
        float len = std::sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
        if (len <= 1e-6f) return false;
        F = s.gravMax - len / s.gravRadius * (s.gravMax - s.gravMin);
        ux = dx / len; uy = dy / len;
    } else {
        ux = -s.pbody->RotCol1Y(); uy = s.pbody->RotCol1X();
        float h = s.gravExt * 0.5f;
        float px = s.pbody->PosX() + ux * h - tx, py = s.pbody->PosY() + uy * h - ty;
        float d = std::sqrt(px * px + py * py);
        F = s.gravExt > 0 ? s.gravMax - d / s.gravExt * (s.gravMax - s.gravMin) : s.gravMax;
    }
    float mag = F * mass * 0.1f;
    if (const char* gd = std::getenv("AB_GRAVDBG")) { static int gn = 0; if ((gd[0] == '1' || s.name == gd) && gn++ < 40) std::fprintf(stderr, "GRAV %s -> %s min=%g max=%g rad=%g ext=%g F=%g dir=%g,%g mass=%g\n", s.name.c_str(), t.name.c_str(), s.gravMin, s.gravMax, s.gravRadius, s.gravExt, F, ux, uy, mass); }
    // Space 1.1.0 for iPhone (0x37522): the bird factor is not used by box sensors, and it fades by 2 a second (the PC's 1.3); a
    // gravity box (Bonus191) pulled birds gravityForceMultiplier (3.28) times too hard
    if (t.isBird && !(phoneSpaceGravity && s.gravRadius <= -1)) {
        if (phoneSpaceGravity && timer >= 0) { float m = gravityForceMultiplier - timer * 2.0f; if (m > 1) mag *= m; }
        else mag *= BirdGravityFactor(timer);
    }
    else if (t.revertGravity) mag *= Tn("gravity.revertFactor", -0.1f);
    else if (t.revertMulti) {
        if (std::sqrt(tvx * tvx + tvy * tvy) >= t.revertMaxSpeed) return false;
        mag *= t.revertMult;
    }
    fx = ux * mag; fy = uy * mag;
    return true;
}

// 0x41e440: water. `w` is the water sensor (+0x11c minimum, +0x120 maximum, +0x124 radius = ids 25..27, +0x15e = id 34), `o` the object in it.
// The force points at the water's centre (a circle) or straight up (a box), is the buoyancy mass * 0.1 * (density of the object - density of the water)
// scaled from the maximum at the surface to the minimum at full depth, fades out inside the top 1.5 world units of the water, and acts a little to
// the side of the centre when the object leans (so that it rights itself); a drag of mass * coefficient * -velocity always applies.
void PhysicsWorld::ApplyWater(PhysObject& w, PhysObject& o) {
    const float g = gameWorldScale, PI_ = 3.14159265f;
    float wMin = w.gravMin, wMax = w.gravMax, wRad = w.gravRadius;
    float mass = o.pbody->Mass(), ang = o.pbody->Angle();
    float dx = w.pbody->PosX() - o.pbody->PosX(), dy = w.pbody->PosY() - o.pbody->PosY();
    float len = std::sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
    float fVar2 = std::min(wRad, len);
    bool bird = o.isBird && o.birdGravReduce < 0;                       // controlled and no collision yet
    float ux = dx, uy = dy;
    if (len >= 1.1920929e-07f) { ux = 1.0f / len * dx; uy = 1.0f / len * dy; }
    float fVar3 = wRad;
    if (!w.isCircle) {                                                   // a box of water: straight up, depth below its top edge
        fVar3 = w.boxH;
        ux = 0; uy = 1;
        float depth = (fVar3 * 0.5f + w.pbody->PosY()) - o.pbody->PosY();
        if (depth <= 0) depth = 0;
        fVar2 = std::min(depth, fVar3);
    }
    if (w.stopOnExit) { ux = 0; uy = 1; fVar2 = 0; }                     // +0x15e (id 34)
    float F = mass * Tn("water.buoyancy", 0.1f) * (o.waterDensity - w.waterDensity) * (wMax - (wMax - wMin) * (fVar2 / fVar3));
    if (bird) F = waterForceMultiplier * F;
    float band = std::min(g * Tn("water.band", 1.5f), fVar3);
    float offX = 0, offY = 0;
    if (fVar3 - band < fVar2 && !bird) {
        float ratio = (fVar3 - fVar2) / band;
        F = ratio * F;
        float vx = std::cos(ang), vy = std::sin(ang);
        if (o.boxW < o.boxH) { vx = std::cos(ang + PI_ * 0.5f); vy = std::sin(ang + PI_ * 0.5f); }
        float dot = vx * ux + vy * uy;
        offX = dot * vx * (1 - ratio); offY = dot * vy * (1 - ratio);
    }
    if (o.keepOrientation) { offX = std::cos(ang - PI_ * 0.5f) * Tn("water.keepOrientationOffset", 0.25f); offY = std::sin(ang - PI_ * 0.5f) * Tn("water.keepOrientationOffset", 0.25f); }
    float size = g;
    if (!o.isCircle) {                                                   // the aspect ratio of a box moves the push point further out
        float lo = std::min(o.boxW, o.boxH), hi = std::max(o.boxW, o.boxH);
        size = (lo > 0 ? hi / lo : 1.0f) * Tn("water.boxPushFactor", 0.25f) * g;
    }
    float vx = o.pbody->VelX(), vy = o.pbody->VelY();
    if (-g * Tn("water.pushSpeedLimit", 15.0f) < uy * vy + ux * vx || bird)
        o.pbody->ApplyForce(F * ux, F * uy, o.pbody->PosX() + size * offX, o.pbody->PosY() + size * offY);
    float drag = (bird ? birdWaterDrag : objectWaterDrag) * mass;        // always, whatever the depth
    o.pbody->ApplyForce(-vx * drag, -vy * drag, o.pbody->PosX(), o.pbody->PosY());
}

int PhysicsWorld::SensorPair(PhysObject* sen, PhysObject* other, bool enter) {
    if (enter) sensorPairs_.push_back({sen, other});
    else {
        bool found = false;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < sensorPairs_.size(); i++)
            if (sensorPairs_[i].first == sen && sensorPairs_[i].second == other) { sensorPairs_.erase(sensorPairs_.begin() + i); found = true; break; }
        if (!found) return -1;
    }
    int left = 0;
    for (const auto& pr : sensorPairs_) if (pr.second == other) left++;
    return left;
}

// 0x474250 / 0x46f720: every awake object applies the force of each gravitation sensor it currently touches (the contact list, not a distance scan)
void PhysicsWorld::ApplyGravitySensors(float dt) {
    ApplyOwnGravity();
    // 0x483500 goes through the objects and, for each one whose body is awake, 0x474250 walks that object's own list of touching sensors from the last
    // entry to the first (the order matters for the rounding of the summed force). A sleeping object is not pulled at all, whatever its sensors do, and
    // an object of kind 5 or 7 is skipped. 0x46f720 only tests the sensor kind (+0x15c == 2): the flag set by parameter 22 (+0x19f) is stored but never read.
    for (size_t i = sensorPairs_.size(); i-- > 0;) {
        PhysObject& s = *sensorPairs_[i].first; PhysObject& t = *sensorPairs_[i].second;
        if (const char* gd = std::getenv("AB_GRAVDBG")) { static int pn = 0; if (s.name == gd && pn++ < 30) std::fprintf(stderr, "GPAIR %s -> %s kind=%d tkind=%d awake=%d static=%d\n", s.name.c_str(), t.name.c_str(), s.sensorKind, t.sensorKind, t.pbody ? (int)t.pbody->IsAwake() : -1, t.pbody ? (int)t.pbody->IsStatic() : -1); }
        if (!s.pbody || !t.pbody || s.sensorKind != 2 || t.sensorKind == 5 || t.sensorKind == 7 || !t.pbody->IsAwake()) continue;
        if (t.pbody->IsStatic()) continue;
        if (starWarsRules && !s.gravOn) continue;                       // 0x423270 only acts for a sensor with parameter 22 set
        if (starWarsRules && s.isWater) { ApplyWater(s, t); continue; }
        if (s.gravMask > -1 && t.gravCat > -1 && (s.gravMask & t.gravCat) == 0) continue;
        float fx, fy;
        if (GravityPull(s, t, t.pbody->PosX(), t.pbody->PosY(), t.pbody->VelX(), t.pbody->VelY(), t.birdGravReduce, t.pbody->Mass(), fx, fy))
            t.pbody->ApplyForce(fx, fy, t.pbody->PosX(), t.pbody->PosY());
    }
    // 0x483537: the exe goes through its objects in name order and advances an object's timer right after that object's own turn, so the sensors
    // (names like BLOCK_SENSOR_...) have pulled the bird with the old value before it runs by one fixed step
    for (const auto& bo : objects_)
        if (starWarsRules) { if ((bo->isBird || bo->affectedByForceMult) && bo->birdGravReduce >= 0) bo->birdGravReduce += dt; }   // 0x432f5c: +0x138 grows while it is 0 or more for controlled / force-multiplied objects
        else if (bo->isBird && bo->birdGravReduce >= 0) bo->birdGravReduce += dt;
}

// ---- gravity of one object. Box2D 2.2 applies the world's gravity to every body (b2Body::SetGravityScale only exists from 2.3), so an object
// with a gravity of its own gets the difference as a force: m * (own - world). Together with the world's gravity the body then accelerates by
// exactly its own value. Only awake dynamic bodies are pushed (a body that sleeps is woken when the gravity is set); the force goes through the
// centre of mass, so the body does not start to spin.
bool PhysicsWorld::SetOwnGravityVector(const std::string& n, float gx, float gy) {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (!o) return false;
    o->ownGravityMode = 1; o->ownGravityX = gx; o->ownGravityY = gy;
    if (o->pbody && !o->pbody->IsStatic()) o->pbody->SetAwake(true);
    return true;
}

bool PhysicsWorld::SetOwnGravityScale(const std::string& n, float scale) {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (!o) return false;
    o->ownGravityMode = 2; o->ownGravityScale = scale;
    if (o->pbody && !o->pbody->IsStatic()) o->pbody->SetAwake(true);
    return true;
}

bool PhysicsWorld::ResetOwnGravity(const std::string& n) {
    PhysObject* o = Find(n);
    if (!o) return false;
    o->ownGravityMode = 0;
    return true;
}

bool PhysicsWorld::GetOwnGravity(const std::string& n, int& mode, float& gx, float& gy, float& scale) const {
    for (const auto& o : objects_)
        if (o->name == n) {
            float wx, wy; GetGravity(wx, wy);
            mode = o->ownGravityMode; scale = o->ownGravityScale;
            if (mode == 1) { gx = o->ownGravityX; gy = o->ownGravityY; }
            else if (mode == 2) { gx = wx * scale; gy = wy * scale; }
            else { gx = wx; gy = wy; scale = 1; }
            return true;
        }
    return false;
}

void PhysicsWorld::ApplyOwnGravity() {
    float wx, wy;
    GetGravity(wx, wy);
    for (const auto& o : objects_) {
        if (o->ownGravityMode == 0 || !o->pbody || o->pbody->IsStatic() || !o->pbody->IsAwake()) continue;
        float gx = o->ownGravityMode == 1 ? o->ownGravityX : wx * o->ownGravityScale;
        float gy = o->ownGravityMode == 1 ? o->ownGravityY : wy * o->ownGravityScale;
        float m = o->pbody->Mass();
        o->pbody->ApplyForce(m * (gx - wx), m * (gy - wy), o->pbody->PosX(), o->pbody->PosY());
    }
}

// predictCollision: what a hit between two objects would do. The contact comes from the real shapes (the closest points of every fixture pair, so a box
// corner or a polygon edge is found where it really is); the hit is the one Box2D's contact solver computes for a single contact point: a normal impulse
```
